title: Auto TLS
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Automatic HTTPS certificates through ACME, with CertMagic (Caddy's certificate engine). PocketBase already gets Let's Encrypt certificates for serve example.com . Auto TLS takes over that job and adds other certificate authorities, extra domains and wildcard certificates. Status: stable on a multisite host, beta on a single app. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Auto TLS
heading: Install
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone and off by default . Turn it on with --autotls (or auto: true in pocketone.yaml ). It only does something when the app serves HTTPS, that is with serve or --https ; on plain HTTP it stays idle, and without it PocketBase's own certificates are used as before. In your own Go build, register it before the app starts: import ( "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" ) app := pocketbase.New() extkit.MustRegister(app, autotls.NewApp(autotls.Config{Auto: true, Email: "ops@example.com"})) app.Start()

title: Auto TLS
heading: Command-line flags
text: pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsEmail ops@example.com pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsDomains " .example.com" --autotlsDNS cloudflare # token in $CF_API_TOKEN --autotls false Turn it on. --autotlsEmail ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. --autotlsCA letsencrypt letsencrypt , letsencrypt-staging , zerossl , or an ACME directory URL. --autotlsDomains Extra domains, obtained at start (comma separated). Wildcards need --autotlsDNS . --autotlsDNS DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges. Only cloudflare is supported. --autotlsDNSTokenEnv CF_API_TOKEN Environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token.

title: Auto TLS
heading: pocketone.yaml
text: The autotls section sets the defaults for those flags. Flags win over the file. autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com ca: letsencrypt domains: [" .example.com"] # wildcards need dns dns: provider: cloudflare api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN # read from the .env beside pocketone.yaml storage is only in the file: where certificates are kept (default pb_data/.autotls ). The DNS token can be given as api_token (write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file) or through api_token_env , the name of an environment variable. api_token is only used when --autotlsDNS names the same provider as the file. The Cloudflare token needs permission to edit the zone's DNS. There are no dashboard settings.

title: Auto TLS
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Use
text: Once on, there's nothing to click. Start the app as usual with serve (or --https ): Which hostnames get a certificate. The domains given to serve and their www. variants, issued on the first request for each, plus --autotlsDomains , obtained at start. Any other hostname is refused at the TLS handshake, so a random Host can't trigger issuance. How they're proved. TLS-ALPN-01 on the HTTPS port, or DNS-01 when a DNS provider is set (needed for wildcards). HTTP-01 isn't used on a single app, because port 80 is PocketBase's redirect server. Renewal is automatic. Where they're stored. pb_data/.autotls by default, separate from PocketBase's own .autocert_cache . Settings are checked at start, before anything touches the network. A wildcard domain without a DNS provider, a Cloudflare provider without a token, or an unknown provider stops the app with an error such as: tls.domains: wildcard " .example.com" needs a DNS provider (tls.dns); per-hostname certificates work without one With debug logging, the start shows autotls: CertMagic serves HTTPS certificates with the CA and extra domains. Use --autotlsCA letsencrypt-staging while testing, so failed attempts don't count against Let's Encrypt's rate limits.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Multisite hosts
text: On a multisite host (any runtime: pocker or docker), the stock pocketone binary runs autotls.New() , a host extension that gets certificates for every instance the host serves. It's configured by the same autotls section: autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com storage: ./pb_root/.pocker-certs # default: .pocker-certs in the runtime's instance root domains: [" .example.com", "example.com"] dns: { provider: cloudflare, api_token_env: CF_API_TOKEN } # only needed for wildcards Without dns , every hostname the instance source maps gets its own certificate on its first TLS handshake, with any DNS host and no API token. Hostnames no instance serves never trigger issuance. Challenges include HTTP-01 on the host's port 80, as well as TLS-ALPN-01 and DNS-01. Certificate files ( server.tls.cert / key ) stay a core host feature. Setting both files and auto is an error. Certificates belong to the host, not to instances; the single-app extension ( NewApp ) is a separate type so it never runs per instance.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Building on Auto TLS
text: autotls.New() is a host extension ( multisite.Extension ) that provides the tls/v1 contract when auto is on. A host adds it to its host extensions (a pocker.Server built by hand takes it in Extensions too): h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Extensions: []multisite.Extension{autotls.New()}}) AutoTLS.Config can be set in Go before the server starts; the autotls section is read only when Auto is false there. autotls.SupportedDNSProviders lists the dns.provider values it understands.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Example
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone : examples/pocketone/main.go registers it with the other default extensions.

title: Auto TLS
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls . On a single app, an OnServe hook swaps the TLS config of PocketBase's HTTPS server for CertMagic's. PocketBase's own host policy (the serve domains and www. ) decides which on-demand hostnames are allowed. The certificate manager stops when the app terminates. TLS 1.2 is the minimum; h2 and http/1.1 are offered, and acme-tls/1 stays on for TLS-ALPN challenges. A wildcard in domains covers one level ( .example.com covers a.example.com , not a.b.example.com ).

title: Auto TLS
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Backups
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Restore an app to a moment from its own backups. Ask for "Tuesday 15:00" and the app restores the latest backup made at or before it, wherever its backups are kept (pb_data/backups or S3). Every app gets this; with PITR on, PITR answers instead and restores any second in its window. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Backups
heading: Install
text: Backups is built into pocketone and on by default ; there's nothing to install. In your own Go build: extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{backups.New()}, nil, nil) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/backups .

title: Backups
heading: Configure
text: There's nothing to configure: it reads the backups PocketBase already makes (Settings → Backups, including the automatic schedule and S3). An app turns it off with extensions: { backups: { enabled: false } } .

title: Backups
heading: Use
text: It's the default provider of the restore/v1 contract: # what can be restored (superuser token) curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1 # restore the latest backup at or before a moment curl -X POST -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"at":"2026-11-10T15:00:00Z"}' https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1/restore The answer names the backup it restores. The app restarts to apply it, as a restore from Settings → Backups does. In the dashboard, Settings → Backups has a "Restore to a moment" section (restore/v1's own screen) that shows which backup a moment uses. Agents get the same through MCP ( restore_points , restore_restore_to ).

title: Backups
heading: Integrations
text: PITR Also provides restore/v1, at any second rather than at backup times; when it's on for an app, Backups steps aside. S3 Fallback Backups kept on the host's storage are listed and restored the same way. Contracts restore/v1 is the contract; any extension or host can provide it instead.

title: Backups
heading: Example
text: // Command example is a PocketBase app whose restore/v1 comes from its backups: create a backup in the dashboard // (Settings → Backups), then curl -H "Authorization: " http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/_c/restore/v1 // lists it, and POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore with {"at": " "} restores the latest backup before it. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/backups" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{backups.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Backups
heading: How it works
text: Points lists the backups filesystem ( app.NewBackupsFilesystem() ), newest first, by each file's time. RestoreTo picks the newest backup at or before the moment and runs PocketBase's own RestoreBackup , which swaps pb_data and restarts the app.

title: Backups
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Bulk Mail
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Campaigns to your app's own users, from the dashboard. You pick who gets the mail with a collection, a view or SQL, write the message, and Bulk Mail sends it at a steady pace through your app's mail settings. It adds one-click unsubscribe, keeps a list of addresses that must never be mailed again, and handles bounces and spam complaints. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Install
text: Bulk Mail is built into pocketone and on for every app. Nothing is sent until a superuser starts a campaign. In your own Go build, register the extension before the app starts. Bind it into the JS runtime too if you want $bulkmail in pb_hooks : mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{Rate: 5, Daily: 5000}) app := pocketbase.New() extkit.MustRegister(app, mail) jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { extkit.BindJS(app, rt, mail) }}) app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Configure
text: There is no pocketone.yaml section or command-line flag. The limits are fixed in the binary; pocketone uses the defaults: Per second 5 The most messages this app sends per second. A campaign can only lower it. Per day 5,000 The most messages this app sends per UTC day, across all campaigns. In a custom build, set them with bulkmail.Config{Rate, Daily} . Daily: bulkmail.NoBulkMail forbids sending; the screens then say so.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Settings → Mail
text: Campaigns send through the app's own mail settings and from its sender, both set on Settings → Mail . Below that form there's a Bulk mail section: Postal address : shown in every campaign footer. Anti-spam laws require one. Unsubscribe mailbox : optional. Adds a mailto: alternative to the List-Unsubscribe header. Bounces and complaints (click to open): Amazon SES (SNS) endpoint : the URL to subscribe to the SNS topic your SES identity sends bounce and complaint notifications to. Allowed SNS topic ARNs : comma separated. Empty accepts any topic with a valid AWS signature. Generic webhook and Webhook secret : for other providers. The webhook is off until you set a secret. The section also shows this app's limits and how many messages it sent today. Click Save bulk mail settings . Unsubscribe links and the feedback URLs are built from Settings → Application → Application URL , so set it to the address people reach your app on. The settings are stored in the app's database (a _params row), so they go along with its backups. Secrets are never shown again after saving.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Use
text: The dashboard gets a Mail link in its menu, with two pages: Campaigns and Suppressions . Only superusers see them.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Write a campaign
text: Open Mail and click New campaign . It starts as a draft for verified users of users . Fill in Name , Subject and Body . Under Audience , choose who gets it: Filter : a Collection (or a view), an optional Filter in the same syntax as API rules, and the Email field that holds the address (an email or text field, or a view's computed column). SQL : a read-only SELECT that returns an email column. Every other column is available to the message. Click Count recipients to see how many match, how many are suppressed, and a few sample addresses. Optional: Vars (JSON) for values used in the message, a Schedule (UTC) , and Max per second to send slower than the app's limit. Click Save changes . Preview shows the message for one recipient; Send test mails it to the Test address . A view is the easy way to build a dynamic audience: it picks who gets mail and computes the columns the message uses. The example creates one called newsletter_audience .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Placeholders
text: In the subject and body: {{record.field}} : a field or column of the recipient's row, for example {{record.name}} . {{email}} , {{campaign.name}} and {{unsubscribe_url}} . Campaign vars: {"promo": "X"} gives {{promo}} . A var can be computed once when sending starts: {"count": {"sql": "SELECT COUNT( ) AS value FROM users"}} . {{if record.field}}…{{else}}…{{end}} blocks, and {{if !record.field}} for the opposite. Values are HTML-escaped in the body. An unsubscribe footer with your postal address is always added.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Send
text: Click Send (or Schedule when a time is set) and confirm. The campaign page shows its status and progress (sent, queued, skipped, failed), and a Recipients table you can filter by status. While it runs you can Pause , Resume or Cancel it. Every address is queued once per campaign. Sending a finished campaign again mails only new matches. A message counts as sent only once the mail server accepts it, so a restart doesn't send twice or skip anyone. A permanent error (SMTP 5xx) fails that recipient. Other errors are retried, up to three attempts. A campaign pauses itself when more than 5% of its sends fail after the first 100, or when spam complaints pass 0.3% of its sends (at least 3). The reason shows next to its status.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Suppressions
text: Mail → Suppressions lists the addresses that never receive campaign mail, whatever the audience says. Unsubscribes, permanent bounces and complaints are added automatically. Click Add address to add one by hand, a row to edit or delete it, or Export CSV to download the list.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Unsubscribing
text: Every message has a signed unsubscribe link and the List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click headers that Gmail and Yahoo require for bulk senders. Opening the link shows a confirm button, so link scanners can't unsubscribe anyone. The one-click request from a mail provider unsubscribes directly.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Try it locally
text: In dev mode with SMTP off, pocketone catches every mail, bulk mail included, in an inbox at http://127.0.0.1:8025: pocketone serve --dev

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Works with
text: Pocker Add the same extension value to srv.Extensions and every instance gets Bulk Mail. Each instance can override its limits (below). $bulkmail only reaches the instance's own data, so it's safe for untrusted tenants. Mailtrap In dev mode with SMTP off, campaign mail lands in the local inbox instead of being sent.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Per-instance settings (pocker)
text: Each instance's extensions.bulkmail settings apply over the Config given to bulkmail.New : instances: id: abc extensions: { bulkmail: { rate: 2, daily: 1000 } } id: free-plan-app extensions: { bulkmail: { daily: 0 } } # may not send bulk mail id: other extensions: { bulkmail: { enabled: false } } # no Bulk Mail at all

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Go API
text: bulkmail.For(app) returns the app's service: Start , StartLimit , Pause , Resume , Cancel , Preview , Test , CountAudience , Suppress , Unsuppress , IsSuppressed , Unsubscribe , UnsubscribeURL , Limits , and the hooks: OnSend fires before every campaign message (not test sends). Change the message, or return an error to fail that recipient. OnUnsubscribe fires when someone unsubscribes through a link or the one-click header. OnFeedback fires for each bounce or complaint a provider reports. Config.Mailer swaps the mail client, for example for a platform relay. Config.PublicURL sets the base of unsubscribe links instead of the Application URL.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: JS API
text: $bulkmail in pb_hooks : $bulkmail.start(id, [limit]) // limit: queue only the next N new recipients $bulkmail.pause(id); $bulkmail.resume(id); $bulkmail.cancel(id) $bulkmail.test(id, [to]); $bulkmail.preview(id, [email]) $bulkmail.count({collection, filter, email_field} {sql}) // {count, suppressed, sample} $bulkmail.suppress(email, [reason]); $bulkmail.unsuppress(email); $bulkmail.isSuppressed(email) $bulkmail.unsubscribe(email, [campaignId]); $bulkmail.unsubscribeURL(email, [campaignId]) $bulkmail.limits() // {rate, daily, sentToday} React to activity with record hooks on the collections below, for example onRecordAfterCreateSuccess((e) = { … }, "_bulkmail_suppressions") .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: API: contracts
text: Bulk Mail has no routes of its own. Its API is three contracts it provides, plus a section in settings/v1 ( ?extension=bulkmail : sender details, limits and the feedback endpoint URLs; secrets are never returned): bulkmail/v1 Count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign (superusers). mail.suppression/v1 The suppression list (check, suppress, unsuppress) and the unsubscribe link in every message (public, signed). Bulk Mail keeps it by default; when another extension provides it, Bulk Mail asks that one before queueing and before each send. mail.feedback/v1 Bounce and complaint reports from SES (SNS) or a webhook (public; X-Feedback-Secret ). Any extension can act on them. Campaigns and suppressions are created and edited through the regular records API. A campaign's from_name and from_address override the app's sender, but only through the records API, JS or Go (the dashboard doesn't show them), since the app's mail account can usually send only as identities it has verified.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Example
text: example/main.go runs one app with bulk mail: the Mail page, campaigns to the app's own users and $bulkmail in JS hooks. Run it with go run ./example serve --dev from this folder; the dev mail trap at http://127.0.0.1:8025 catches every mail. // Command example runs one PocketOne app with bulk mail: a "Mail" page in the dashboard, campaigns to the app's // own users, and $bulkmail in JS hooks. // // Run it in dev mode: while SMTP is off, PocketOne's dev mail trap catches every mail (bulk mail included) and // shows it at http://127.0.0.1:8025, with nothing else to install: // // go run ./example serve --dev // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit/js" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" registerDemoView(app) // a "newsletter_audience" view to use as a campaign audience (demo.go) // the same extension value pocker would host on every instance (srv.Extensions = append(srv.Extensions, mail)) mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{ Rate: 5, // messages per second Daily: 5000, // messages per day; bulkmail.NoBulkMail forbids sending }) extkit.MustRegister(app, mail) jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{ OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { extkit.BindJS(app, rt, mail) }, // $bulkmail in JS hooks }) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Bulk Mail
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail , an extkit extension. example/main.go runs one app with Bulk Mail ( go run ./example serve --dev ). The audience is resolved when sending starts and queued into a ledger first (one row per campaign and address, unique). A background sender then mails one message at a time through the app's mail client, at the lower of the app's rate and the campaign's. SQL audiences and SQL vars run with SQLite's query_only on, inside a transaction that is always rolled back. Unsubscribe links are signed with HMAC and a per-app secret, generated on first use. SES feedback: SNS signatures are verified, and signing certificates are fetched only from sns. .amazonaws.com . Permanent bounces and complaints go on the suppression list.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Data
text: _bulkmail_campaigns Content, audience, vars, status, counters, schedule. _bulkmail_sends The ledger: campaign, email, status ( queued , sent , skipped , failed ), reason, attempts. _bulkmail_suppressions Addresses that never receive campaign mail, with the reason. All are superuser-only system collections with fixed collection and field ids ( schema.go ). LegacyJSMigration() emits a PocketBase JS migration that creates the same collections, for apps that move onto this schema before they run this extension.

heading: License
text: MIT

title: Bundle
text: Version 0.1.0 · Owners: @benallfree Ship an app's files inside the binary instead of folders on disk: its JS hooks ( pb_hooks ), migrations ( pb_migrations ) and public files ( pb_public ). Nothing is written to disk and nothing on disk can override them. PocketHost's mothership uses it for its own hooks. Formerly jsembed . Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Bundle
heading: Install
text: Bundle is not in the pocketone binary. Add it to your own Go build: embed the folders, pass the hooks and migrations to jsvm as extensions, and serve the public files. //go:embed hooks migrations public var files embed.FS hooks, _ := fs.Sub(files, "hooks") migrations, _ := fs.Sub(files, "migrations") public, _ := fs.Sub(files, "public") jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{ Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks), bundle.Migrations(migrations)}, }) bundle.Public(app, public, true) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bundle .

title: Bundle
heading: Configure
text: Nothing to configure. List only what you bundle: without bundle.Hooks , hooks still come from HooksDir on disk, and the same for migrations.

title: Bundle
heading: Use
text: Hooks: .pb.js files come from the FS's root only. HooksDir is ignored, nothing is written to it, and hooks aren't watched. Migrations: files come from the FS's root only; MigrationsDir is ignored. require() : __hooks is the virtual root /pb_embedded/pb_hooks . Paths under it, and relative paths, load from the hooks FS. Everything else is "module not found": absolute disk paths, .. escapes, node_modules . JS that reads files itself ( $os.readFile(__hooks + ...) ) gets "no such file", since the root doesn't exist on disk. Public files: bundle.Public(app, fsys, indexFallback) serves the FS at GET /{path...} like pb_public , unless the app has its own route there. With indexFallback , unknown paths serve index.html (single-page apps).

title: Bundle
heading: Integrations
text: JSVM Hooks and Migrations are jsvm extensions ( HookFiles , Modules , MigrationFiles ).

title: Bundle
heading: Example
text: // Command example serves its JS hooks and public files from files embedded in the binary: no pb_hooks or pb_public // folder on disk. // // go run ./example serve // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hello // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/ package main import ( "embed" "io/fs" "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bundle" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm" ) //go:embed hooks public var files embed.FS func main() { hooks, err := fs.Sub(files, "hooks") if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } public, err := fs.Sub(files, "public") if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks)}}) bundle.Public(app, public, true) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Bundle
heading: How it works
text: Hooks implements jsvm's HookFiles and Modules : the engine asks it for the hook files and for every module require() resolves, and it serves only paths under the virtual root, from the FS. Migrations implements MigrationFiles . Public binds the static route with apis.Static at the lowest priority, as PocketBase does for pb_public .

title: Bundle
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Cache
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Extensions and apps often compute the same thing many times: a rendered page, an answer from another API, a compiled module. Cache gives them named buckets to keep those results in, from one store in your app's process, with an optional folder on disk for more than fits in memory. Each bucket has its own caps, and you can change them without touching the code that uses them. On a multisite host the store is shared by every instance: one memory budget and one disk tier for all of them. Each instance still sees only its own buckets, and identical bytes (the same compiled template, the same .wasm file) are kept once however many instances or keys hold them. Cache provides cache/v1. Code that caches talks only to that contract, so a cache shared between servers (Redis, Memcached) can replace this one later without any of it changing. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Cache
heading: Install
text: Cache is built into pocketone and on by default; there's nothing to install. Turn it off with cache: {enabled: false} in pocketone.yaml . In your own Go build it comes with the standard set, or on its own: extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{cache.New(cache.Config{})}, nil, nil)

title: Cache
heading: Configure
text: Nothing to configure: the store has 128 MiB of memory for every bucket together, and each bucket takes the caps its code asks for. To change them, add a cache section to pocketone.yaml . The top keys size the store; defaults fill in what a bucket's code leaves unset; buckets set a named bucket's caps over what its code asks for: cache: max_memory: 512MiB # the store: every bucket together disk_path: cache # overflow for what memory evicts; leave out for memory only max_disk: 10GiB defaults: ttl: 10m buckets: pages.compiled: max_memory: 64MiB # one app's bucket The store: max_memory Memory for every bucket together (default 128MiB) max_items Most distinct values kept in memory; identical bytes count once eviction Which values leave memory first when the store is full: lru (default), mru , fifo , lifo disk_path Turns on the disk tier there, in a p1cache folder that is emptied when the process starts. Relative paths are under pb_data on a single app, and under the working directory on a multisite host max_disk Size of the disk tier (default 1GiB) Each bucket ( defaults and buckets. ): max_items Most entries the bucket holds max_memory Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds; a value it shares with others counts in full eviction Which of its entries go first when the bucket is full ttl How long an entry lives unless its code says otherwise Sizes take KiB , MiB , GiB (or KB , MB , GB ); durations take s , m , h . A disk tier inside pb_data is part of your backups (as throwaway files). To keep it out, give disk_path an absolute folder outside pb_data .

title: Cache
heading: cache:
text: The cache (cache/v1): one store for every app in the process (memory, disk tier), and caps per bucket. enabled bool Turns the cache off when false; extensions then run uncached. eviction string Which values leave memory first when the store is full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. max_items int Most distinct values kept in memory (identical bytes count once). max_memory int Memory for every bucket together, such as 512MiB. Default 128MiB. disk_path string Turns on a disk tier there for what memory evicts (in a p1cache folder, emptied when the process starts). Relative: under pb_data on a single app, the working directory on a multisite host. max_disk int Size of the disk tier, such as 10GiB. Default 1GiB. defaults.eviction string Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. defaults.max_items int Most entries the bucket holds. defaults.max_memory int Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds, such as 32MiB (shared values count in full). defaults.ttl int How long an entry lives unless the code says otherwise, such as 10m. buckets map of object Caps per bucket name, over what its code asks for.

title: Cache
heading: Use
text: Nothing to click. Values evicted from memory move to the disk tier when there is one, and a read brings them back. The cache starts empty with the process, disk tier included. On a multisite host, an instance that restarts or sleeps keeps its entries: the store belongs to the host.

title: Cache
heading: Integrations
text: Pocker Every instance shares the host's one store (its memory, its disk tier), and sees only its own buckets: keys live under the instance's id. An instance that sleeps keeps its entries, so it wakes to a warm cache. An instance's extensions.cache may set enabled , defaults and buckets for itself; the store's keys are the host's only. Docker Each container runs its own pocketone , so it has its own store.

title: Cache
heading: Building on Cache
text: Open a bucket through cache/v1 at serve time, keep it, and get and set keys: b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "myext.answers", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 1000, TTL: 10 time.Minute}) Declare cache/v1 in WorksWith : when nothing provides it, Open returns a bucket that keeps nothing, so your code runs uncached. Name buckets after your extension so they never collide. Cache provides cache/v1 as the default: another extension that provides it (a Redis cache, say) replaces it without any providers: line.

title: Cache
heading: Example
text: A PocketBase app with one bucket, example.slow . GET /slow takes a second the first time and answers from the cache for the next minute. // Command example is a PocketBase app with cache/v1 and one bucket, "example.slow". GET /slow takes a second the first // time and answers from the cache for the next minute: // // go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090 // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/slow # slow // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/slow # cached // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "net/http" "time" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/cache" cachev1 "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/cache/v1" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{cache.New(cache.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se core.ServeEvent) error { b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "example.slow", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 100, TTL: time.Minute}) if err != nil { return err } se.Router.GET("/slow", func(e core.RequestEvent) error { ctx := e.Request.Context() if v, ok, _ := b.Get(ctx, "answer"); ok { return e.String(http.StatusOK, "cached: "+string(v)+"\n") } time.Sleep(time.Second) // the expensive part v := time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339) _ = b.Set(ctx, "answer", []byte(v), 0) return e.String(http.StatusOK, "computed: "+v+"\n") }) return se.Next() }) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Cache
heading: How it works
text: One store per process. Each app's buckets are namespaces in it, / (just / on a single app), so no app can read another's keys. Keys point at values stored by their SHA-256: the same bytes under any number of keys, from any number of instances, are one value with a reference count, and count once against the store's memory and item limits. A value goes when the last key pointing at it does. There are two kinds of eviction. When the store is over its limits, a value leaves memory (by the store's strategy): to the disk tier when there is one, else together with every key pointing at it. When one bucket is over its own caps, one of its keys goes (by the bucket's strategy), and the value only if nothing else points at it. The key index stays in memory and counts against max_memory . The disk tier is overflow for memory: one file per value, named by its hash, written atomically and emptied when the process starts. One lock guards the index, and it's never held across disk IO. One IO goroutine, running only while it has work, writes and removes files in the order the lock decided them. A value waiting to be written stays readable from memory (at most a quarter of max_memory waits; past that, evicted values are dropped). Reads from disk happen off the lock, many readers of one value share one read, and a read is checked against the index again before it's returned, so a key changed meanwhile never gets its old value back. The store is tested against a model under fuzzing (no value deleted, replaced, expired or belonging to another key ever comes back; every count and list stays consistent; the disk tier holds exactly the files it should) and under concurrent load with the race detector.

text: MIT

title: Config
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree PocketOne's config file: pocketone.yaml , with secrets in a .env beside it. Put your app's settings in one file instead of a long line of flags. Each extension has its own section in the file. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Config
heading: Install
text: Config is built into pocketone and always on. Without a pocketone.yaml , nothing changes: every setting keeps its default and the flags work as usual. In your own Go build, load the file before the app is created, so its values can be the flags' defaults: cfg, err := config.Load(config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:])) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } appCfg, _ := config.App.Get() app := pocketbase.NewWithConfig(pocketbase.Config{DefaultDataDir: cfg.ResolvePath(appCfg.Dir)}) app.RootCmd.AddCommand(config.NewCommand(func() config.Options { return config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]) })) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/config . examples/pocketone/main.go shows the full wiring: every app key as a flag default, and the server keys as the serve command's defaults.

title: Config
heading: Where the files are
text: pocketone.yaml is looked for in the working directory, then next to the executable. --config picks another file. The .env is looked for beside the config file (or in the working directory when there is no config file). --env-file picks another one. Relative paths in the file are relative to the file's folder, so it works from any working directory.

title: Config
heading: What goes in it
text: Each top-level key is one section, owned by the extension that uses it. This package owns three: server : how the app listens. http , https and origins are the defaults for serve --http , --https and --origins . app : your app's folders and options: the same settings as the root flags ( --dir , --dev , --hooksDir , --publicDir and the rest), plus env_allow . multisite : add it only to run many instances from one binary (see Integrations); providers: { runtime/v1: [...] } picks which runtimes. server: http: 127.0.0.1:8090 origins: [" "] app: dir: ./pb_data hooks_dir: ./pb_hooks env_allow: [STRIPE_KEY] pitr: retention: 168h Other extensions' sections (such as pitr above) are described on their own pages. pocketone config lists every section your binary knows.

title: Config
heading: Flags win
text: A flag on the command line always wins over the file. The file only changes the defaults.

title: Config
heading: Secrets in the .env
text: Write $VAR or ${VAR} in any value, and keep the secret in the .env : autotls: dns: api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN # .env CF_API_TOKEN=abc123 A name is looked up in the .env first, then in the process environment. $$ is a literal $ . A name that is set nowhere stops the app at startup, with the missing names listed. The .env takes KEY=VALUE lines. Blank lines, # comments and an export prefix are fine. Quote a value to keep its spaces; double quotes also understand \n , \t , \" and \\ . The .env is used only for these references. It is never put in the process environment, so your JS hooks ( $os.getenv ) don't see it, unless you list a name in app.env_allow .

title: Config
heading: app:
text: The single app: data dir, dev mode, encryption, hooks, migrations, public dir, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host. dir string The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. dev bool Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. encryption_env string Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. query_timeout duration Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. hooks_dir string The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. hooks_watch bool Restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. jsvm string The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $tokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. hooks_pool int Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. migrations_dir string The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. automigrate bool Write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. public_dir string The static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. index_fallback bool Serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. env_allow list of string Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none.

title: Config
heading: server:
text: How the binary listens: http, https and CORS origins (single-app mode: the serve command's defaults). http string Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. https string HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. origins list of string Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). plain list of string Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. tls.cert string Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. tls.key string Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. shutdown_timeout duration Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop.

title: Config
heading: See every section
text: pocketone config It prints each section with its description and defaults, as YAML you can copy into your file. For the same list as JSON (each section's name, description, owning extension, and each key with its type and default): pocketone config --json

title: Config
heading: Check your file
text: pocketone config check It reads the file and the .env and reports problems, or a line like: /srv/app/pocketone.yaml: ok (3 sections), secrets from /srv/app/.env With no file it says no config file: defaults only .

title: Config
heading: What stops startup
text: The app won't start, and says why, when the file has: a top-level key no extension in the binary owns (usually a typo); the error lists the sections it knows; the same section twice; a value that doesn't fit its key (for example text where a number goes); a $VAR that is set in neither the .env nor the environment. An empty section ( pitr: with nothing after it) is allowed and means all defaults.

title: Config
heading: Works with
text: Every extension with a section Each extension declares its own section; its values become that extension's defaults or flag defaults. PITR, S3 Redirect and Auto TLS are examples. Pocker and Docker Add a multisite section and pocketone serve runs many instances instead of one app, on the runtimes providers: { runtime/v1: [...] } picks (default: every configured one). The app section and env_allow don't apply then; each instance has its own folder under its runtime's root.

title: Config
heading: The server section with many instances
text: On a multisite host, server has a few more keys: https is the main address, http then redirects plain HTTP to it ( http alone serves plain HTTP), plain lists extra plain-HTTP addresses with no redirect, tls names a certificate and key file (reloaded when they change), and shutdown_timeout limits how long in-flight requests get at stop. multisite: {} server: https: ":443" http: ":80" plain: [":8080"] tls: { cert: /etc/certs/cert.pem, key: /etc/certs/key.pem }

title: Config
heading: Give your extension a section
text: Declare it in your own package with a typed key and defaults: type Config struct { Limit int yaml:"limit" doc:"Requests per minute. The --limit flag wins." } var Section = extkit.NewSection("firewall", Config{Limit: 60}, "Request limits for the app.") cfg, found := firewall.Section.Get() // the defaults with the file's values applied cfg, err := firewall.Section.Require() // fails when the file doesn't have the section An extension reads a section only through its owner's key, so it can read only sections from packages it imports. There is no lookup by name and no access to the raw file. The doc:"…" tag on each field describes the key in pocketone config --json and in the key table on pocketone.dev. config.Load checks every section when the app starts, so a bad value fails early.

title: Config
heading: Example
text: Config is built into pocketone : examples/pocketone/main.go loads pocketone.yaml with it before the app starts and adds the config command.

title: Config
heading: Go API
text: config.FromArgs(args) reads --config and --env-file before the full flag parse. config.Load(opts) finds, reads and checks the files, and makes them the source for every section. config.Read(opts) does the same without checking or installing them. ( Config).ResolvePath(p) makes a relative path from the file absolute, relative to the file's folder. ( Config).AllowEnv(names) copies those .env values into the process environment (what app.env_allow does). config.Describe() returns every section with its keys, types, defaults and docs (the data behind --json ). config.NewCommand(opts) is the config command.

title: Deploy
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Send your project's code to a running app from your own machine: pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_pages , pb_public , packages and the production node_modules tree. Only changed files are uploaded and the app swaps them in; restart applies new migrations and packages. pocketone dev keeps your folder and the app in step both ways and streams the app's logs; pull and logs work the other way. pocketone link https://myapp.example.com # add the remote and sign in (Remotes) pocketone deploy # upload what changed pocketone logs Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Deploy
heading: Install
text: Deploy is built into pocketone and on in both directions: every app it serves accepts deploys from its superusers, and the deploy , dev , pull , logs and restart commands are there to deploy to other apps. There's nothing to install. In your own Go build, register it before the app starts. Remotes gives the commands their remotes and logins, and Tokens lets you deploy with API tokens: app := pocketbase.New() extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{ tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), // optional: API tokens with the deploy scope remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), // remote/v1 (whoami, restart, logs), login deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{}), // deploy/v1 + deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands }, nil, nil) app.Start() The standard set does this for you. The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy . deploy.Config{DisableServer: true} keeps only the commands, for a binary that deploys elsewhere but must not accept deploys.

title: Deploy
heading: Configure
text: There is no pocketone.yaml section, flag or settings screen. Defaults on the receiving app: Who may deploy: superusers. You sign in with pocketone login (see Remotes) or use an API token. A token needs the deploy scope (or no scopes); deploy:read allows reading files and logs only. Where files land: next to pb_data , PocketBase's usual layout ( pb_hooks/ , pb_migrations/ , pb_public/ , node_modules/ beside it). Upload store: uploaded files and past deploys are kept in .pb_deploy/ next to pb_data . It's outside pb_data , so backups skip it, and it's never deployed. On your machine, the commands use the project's remotes and saved logins from Remotes. In CI, set P1_TOKEN (or P1_TOKEN_ ) instead of signing in.

title: Deploy
heading: Use
text: All commands take an optional remote name or URL; without one they use the project's default remote. Run them from your project folder (or any folder below it).

title: Deploy
heading: deploy
text: pocketone deploy # to the default remote pocketone deploy prod -m "fix signup" # to the remote "prod", with a note pocketone deploy --restart # and restart if migrations or packages changed (CI) pocketone deploy --dry-run # list what would be sent, send nothing pocketone deploy --out /tmp/set # write the files to a folder instead You'll see how many files are deployed and how many are uploaded, then a line like Deployed : 3 changed, 0 deleted, 41 unchanged. With nothing changed it says Up to date: no changes. --restart Restart the app after the files are in, when migrations or packages changed. --dry-run List what would be deployed; deploy nothing. --out Write the deploy set to a local folder instead of deploying. -i , --include Add include patterns to the default set. -e , --exclude Exclude patterns ( pb_data is always excluded). --node-modules Ship the production node_modules tree (the default when there's a package.json ). --no-node-modules Don't ship node_modules ; leave the remote's alone. --commit Commit to record. Default: $GITHUB_SHA , $CI_COMMIT_SHA , or git HEAD . -m , --message A note to record with the deploy. -v , --verbose List every file. What's sent: files matching pb_ and pb_ / / except pb_data , plus package.json , bun.lock(b) and patches/ . Dotfiles are included ( pb_public/.well-known ); .git files and symlinks are skipped. Packages: with a package.json , the production node_modules tree is collected the way Node resolves it (hoisted npm and bun, pnpm's store, workspace links; never devDependencies) and shipped as plain files, so plain JS hooks can require npm packages. The remote then owns its root node_modules : packages you no longer ship are removed there. Restarts: files are swapped in while the app runs, each rename atomic, and deploy never restarts the app on its own. pb_pages and pb_public are read from disk on each request, and hooks reload by themselves (PocketBase's --hooksWatch , Pocker's watcher). Migrations and packages apply only when the app starts, so a deploy that changes them says Migrations or packages changed and leaves the restart to you: pass --restart (the app restarts once, after the whole batch is in, and you hear if it fails to start), run pocketone restart , or type r in dev . So does the first deploy that creates pb_hooks , since a watcher only sees folders that existed when the app started.

title: Deploy
heading: restart
text: pocketone restart prod Restarts the app so it applies new migrations and packages, and tells you if it fails to start. An app that isn't running (a sleeping Pocker instance) is left alone; it applies them when it starts.

title: Deploy
heading: dev
text: pocketone dev pocketone dev prod --prefer local # first sync: upload yours where both sides differ Keeps the project folder and the remote in step, both ways, and streams the remote's logs. Stop it with Ctrl+C. pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_pages , pb_public and other pb_ folders both ways package.json , bun.lock(b) , patches/ both ways node_modules uploaded only, when package.json or the lockfile changes pb_data never (it's the app's live data) Your edits go up half a second after you save. Changes on the remote , such as the migrations the dashboard writes when you edit a collection, come down within a few seconds ( --poll , default 5s). dev asks the remote for one hash and only looks further when it changed, so a large pb_public costs nothing while it's quiet. Restarts: dev never restarts the app by itself. Hooks reload by themselves, pages and public files are live on the next request. After you upload a migration or new packages, dev says so: type r and Enter to restart the app and apply them. Migrations that come down are already applied on the remote. Deletes go both ways too. Changed on both sides: your copy wins and is uploaded; the remote's is saved in .pocketone/conflicts/ and dev says so. First run: files that exist on only one side are copied to the other. If a file differs on both sides, dev lists them and asks whether to keep yours or take the remote's; --prefer local remote answers in advance. dev keeps what it last synced in .pocketone/sync.json (add .pocketone/ to .gitignore ). List files to leave out, such as ones your hooks generate, in .pocketoneignore , one gitignore-style pattern per line. --prefer local\ remote First sync: who wins where both sides differ (default: ask). --poll How often to check the remote (default 5s). --push-only Only upload, the way dev used to work. Also used by itself for remotes without two-way sync. --no-logs Don't stream the remote's logs. It takes the same file flags as deploy .

title: Deploy
heading: pull
text: pocketone pull prod # pb_hooks, pb_migrations, pb_pages, pb_public, pb_templates, package.json pocketone pull prod pb_hooks pb_public/index.html pocketone pull prod --dry-run Downloads files from a remote into the project. pb_data is only reachable on an instance that's powered off, so a single app (always running while it answers) refuses it.

title: Deploy
heading: logs
text: pocketone logs prod pocketone logs prod -n 20 Replays the last 100 lines ( -n , --lines , 0 to 1000), then follows. Requests show as GET /url → 200 (1.2 ms) and errors are marked ERR . PocketBase writes its logs in batches, so lines show up a few seconds late. The stream reconnects by itself if it drops.

title: Deploy
heading: Deploy history
text: Every deploy is recorded in the _deploys collection of the receiving app: status, file counts, bytes, commit, message, source, token name, superuser and any error. Superusers can browse it in the dashboard.

title: Deploy
heading: Works with
text: Remotes Gives the commands their remotes, saved logins and CI tokens. The commands find deploy/v1 in the remote's whoami, and restart and logs use its remote/v1 (deploy requires it). OAuth (in Tokens) pocketone login signs in through the browser when the remote runs it. Tokens Deploy registers the deploy and deploy:read scopes, so you can make API tokens for CI that can only deploy or only read. Add remote for --restart and remote:read for dev 's logs. Pocker The same API runs for many instances with your own backend: build it with deploy.New (below). PocketHost does this.

title: Deploy
heading: Building on Deploy
text: Go client. deploy.NewClient(ctx, rc) takes a remote/v1 client ( remoteclient.Open , from ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient) and finds its deploy API. Deploy , Pull , Collect , Watch and NewSyncer (two-way sync: Sync , RemoteChanged ) are the commands' building blocks. Your own host. deploy.New(deploy.Options{Prefix, Backend, Instances, PBRoot, DataRoot, PlatformPaths}) builds the API; mount api.Wrap(next) . Backend decides which instance a request is for ( Lookup(r) ), who it acts as ( Authenticate(r, inst) → Auth{UserID, Scopes, Via, TokenLabel} , an AuthError , or ErrNoAccess for a 404) and records history. Instances is pocker's Manager (stop, swap, start). Serve it as deploy/v1 for the host's instances ( deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances , extkit.HostRoutes in multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes ); restart and logs are the host's remote/v1. Restarts. Your Instances should reload an instance by itself when its pb_hooks change (pocker's Manager does); deploy only restarts through it when a client asks ( Client.Restart , or DeployOptions.Restart ). Discovery. Deploy provides the deploy/v1 contract, which whoami lists, so clients find it at /api/_c/deploy/v1 . A multisite host can provide it for its instances instead.

title: Deploy
heading: Example
text: example/main.go is an app that both accepts deploys and makes them: the deploy API, API tokens, remotes and the deploy commands. Its comment walks through a first deploy against itself. // Command example is a PocketOne app that accepts deploys and can deploy: deploy/v1 (/api/_c/deploy/v1), remote/v1 // (restart, logs), API tokens, and the deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands. // // go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090 # the remote // cd myproject && mkdir pb_hooks && echo 'routerAdd("GET", "/hi", (e) = e.string(200, "hi"))' pb_hooks/main.pb.js // go run ./example link http://127.0.0.1:8090 --email admin@example.com # password: password // go run ./example deploy // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hi // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" // registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you); deploys land next to pb_data exts := []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{})} if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, exts, nil, nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // deployed pb_hooks and pb_migrations if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Deploy
heading: Deploy API
text: deploy/v1, at /api/_c/deploy/v1 (superusers, see Configure): the files only, on an app or a host. Whoami, restart and logs are remote/v1's ( /api/_c/remote/v1 ), which deploy requires. POST /check Takes a manifest, returns the hashes the server is missing. POST /blobs Gzipped PHB1 bundles: [sha256][uint32 length][bytes] …, every hash verified, 64 MB per request. POST /commit Stage, swap in, record. "restartNeeded": true in the answer when migrations or packages wait for a restart; "restart": true in the request restarts after the swap. With "partial": true only the listed files (and "delete" ) change. GET / DELETE /files List or delete files. GET / PUT /files/raw Download or upload one file. GET /tree One folder of the code set ( ?path= , default the root) with a hash over everything below it; hashOnly=1 for just the hash. The protocol is the pockethost npm CLI's, so the same client deploys to PocketOne apps and PocketHost.

title: Deploy
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy . example/main.go is an app that accepts deploys and can deploy (logins from devusers: admin@example.com / password). A deploy is a hash diff: the client sends a manifest, uploads only the missing files in bundles, then commits. On a single app the files are swapped in while it runs; a restart (when a client asks) is app.Restart() , which re-executes the process ( Config.Restart overrides it; not on Windows). Config.Dir and Config.StoreDir move the deploy folder and the upload store; Config.Prefix moves the API. Logs on a single app come from its own _logs table; entries at error level and above are marked as stderr. The node_modules collector is nodemodules , a port of the npm CLI's.

text: MIT

title: Docker
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Run every instance on a host in its own container, with the official PocketBase or PocketOne binary of the version the instance asks for. One host can serve PocketBase 0.23 and 0.36 and PocketOne side by side. Docker is one of the two runtime providers of the multi-instance multisite. The other is Pocker, which runs every instance inside one process. A host runs exactly one of them. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Docker
heading: Install
text: Docker is built into pocketone . It needs a Docker daemon on the same machine; nothing else to install. It's off until pocketone.yaml names it as the provider (below). Then pocketone serve runs the host instead of a single app. In your own Go build, add it to the host's extensions; it provides the runtime/v1 contract when pocketone.yaml has a docker section: h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Extensions: []multisite.Extension{&docker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}}}) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker . Add docker.NewCommand(...) to your root command for the docker seed and docker update commands.

title: Docker
heading: Configure
text: Add a multisite section (host mode) and a docker section to pocketone.yaml . Listeners ( server ), instances ( instances ) and the firewall are the host's sections. With pocker linked too, both run: each instance on the one its record names ( runtime: docker ), else the first that serves its version; providers: { runtime/v1: [docker] } keeps docker alone. multisite: {} docker: image: alpine:3.20 # base image the binaries run in binaries: /var/lib/pocketbase # release binary cache root: /var/lib/instances # one folder per instance: / versions: ["pb:0.23", "pb:0.36", "p1:0.0"] default_version: "pb:0.36. " idle_ttl: 10m max_concurrent_starts: 4 instances: file: ./instances.yaml image , binaries and root are required. Versions. An instance picks its binary with the prefix of its version : pb: is upstream PocketBase, p1: is PocketOne, no prefix means pb: . versions lists the minors the host serves; the newest cached patch that matches wins. A version that isn't listed gets a clear 503. Upstream PocketBase 0.22 and older are refused unless you lower min_upstream and keep those releases in the cache yourself. Per instance ( instances.yaml or a mothership): version , secrets (passed as environment), encryption_key , dev , and dir to put its folder somewhere other than / . An instance with runtime set to anything but docker isn't served here. Limits and hardening are optional: nano_cpus , pids_limit , nofile , cap_drop and no_new_privileges .

title: Docker
heading: docker:
text: Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits). socket string The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. image string Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. binaries string Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. versions list of string The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). root string Folder with one folder per instance ( / ). Required. home string The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. default_version string Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0. . Empty: such instances fail. min_upstream string Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. idle_ttl duration Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. max_concurrent_starts int Containers starting at once. Default 4. start_timeout duration How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. nano_cpus int CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. pids_limit int Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. nofile list of int Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. cap_drop list of string Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. no_new_privileges bool Set no-new-privileges on every container. network string Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. adopt_image string Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager).

title: Docker
heading: Fetch the binaries
text: pocketone docker update # find the latest patch of each docker.versions minor, record and download it pocketone docker seed # download whatever is recorded but not in the cache yet update checks upstream PocketBase releases (ganigeorgiev.com, then the archived GitHub) and PocketOne releases on GitHub, verifies each download against the release's checksums.txt, and records the list in the cache's releases.json . Run it when you want new patches. Nothing is downloaded at request time: when the host starts, any listed release missing from the cache is downloaded in the background. The cache layout is / / /pocketbase for PocketBase (PocketHost's existing layout) and /p1/ / /pocketone for PocketOne.

title: Docker
heading: Run the host
text: pocketone serve A container starts on an instance's first request and is ready when /api/health answers. At most max_concurrent_starts start at once. It stops after idle_ttl without requests. It restarts on its next request when what it runs changed (secrets, version, mounts). A change to routing only doesn't restart it. It stops when the instance is deleted or moves to another edge. Containers keep running when the host restarts; the next process adopts them by their labels.

title: Docker
heading: Hooks and migrations
text: A change in an instance's pb_hooks restarts its container. PocketBase's own hooks watcher stays on too, so a hook file that fails to load is logged and skipped instead of stopping the instance. A request that arrives while the instance restarts waits for it instead of failing; one that lost its connection mid-restart is sent once more if it's safe to repeat (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS without a body). Migrations run when a container boots.

title: Docker
heading: Maintenance
text: Instance folders are ordinary folders under root . To work on one while nothing has it open, a host's Go code calls WithInstanceStopped (below); requests for that instance wait up to 30 s, then get a 503 with Retry-After .

title: Docker
heading: Remote control
text: Containers run stock images with no PocketOne extensions, so the host answers remote/v1 for them at /api/_c/remote/v1/ on each instance's hostname: the pocketone remote commands work the same as against a Pocker instance or a single app. It answers after the host's gates (firewall, rate limits) and blocked check, so a blocked instance's remote/v1 gets the blocked answer and the container stays stopped. GET /api/_c/remote/v1 (whoami) is public and lists remote/v1 . status , restart and logs need a superuser token of that instance ( pocketone remote login with a superuser email and password). The host asks the instance itself to check it. A host with its own accounts sets docker.Provider.RemoteAuth to decide who may call them instead (PocketHost: the instance owner's tokens). remote/v1 is provided on the host's scope, so whoami also lists the other contracts the host provides for its instances (a host's deploy/v1 ). restart replaces the container; logs replays and follows the container's output, the last 1000 lines per instance kept by this host since it started following the container.

title: Docker
heading: Switching provider
text: Docker and Pocker both use / , so switching is a config change. Stop the containers first when leaving docker, since they keep running across a host restart on purpose. Data only moves forward: an instance started on a newer PocketBase than wrote its data is upgraded.

title: Docker
heading: Works with
text: Multisite Docker is a runtime provider of the host: the host routes by hostname, runs the listeners and gates, and hands each request to docker. Pocker The other provider. A host runs one or the other, over the same instance folders. Edge For a fleet: requests for instances on another edge are forwarded there. Mothership Instances (and their versions) come from a mothership instead of a file. Firewall Rate limits and allow lists in front of every instance. Remotes The host provides remote/v1 for every container, so the CLI's whoami, status, restart and logs work.

title: Docker
heading: Building on Docker
text: docker.Provider fields extend the provider from Go: Container adds mounts, environment and labels to each container; Version rewrites an instance's version before the binary is picked; OnLog receives container output (default: the debug log); Versions replaces the versions list (for example a fleet's list from a mothership); MinUpstream replaces min_upstream . Spec (what Container fills in): Binds , Env , Labels , plus Cmd to adjust the command (for example drop a flag an old release lacks) and HealthPath / HealthAnyStatus for the readiness check. VersionsSource : any type with Releases(ctx) decides which releases the host serves, each pinned to its download and sha256. YAMLVersions (the versions key) is the built-in one. Runtime API : docker.New(docker.Config{...}) builds the runtime without the config file. WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) stops an instance, holds its requests and runs fn on its folder (for deploys and restores); StartInstance starts one now; InstanceDir returns its folder. Remote(host, dir) and SuperuserAuth() are the remote/v1 provider and the host-side auth that Provider wires in, for a host built by hand ( remotev1.W.HostHandler(host, multisite.InstanceID, rt.SuperuserAuth(), next) in Host.InstanceRoutes ). Release helpers : ParseVersion , Pick / PickMin , LatestPatches , Update and Seed are what the commands use.

title: Docker
heading: Example
text: A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container, routed by hostname on one listener. With a Docker daemon running, start it from this folder with go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0 . // A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container with the PocketBase or PocketOne // version it asks for, routed by hostname on one listener. // // go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0 // // instances.yaml: // // instances: // - { id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost], version: "pb:0.23. " } // - { id: shop, hosts: [shop.localhost], version: "p1:0.0. " } package main import ( "context" "flag" "log/slog" "os" "os/signal" "strings" "syscall" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite" ) func main() { instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file") data := flag.String("data", "./instances", "folder with one folder per instance") binaries := flag.String("binaries", "./bin", "PocketBase and PocketOne binary cache") versions := flag.String("versions", "pb:0.23,p1:0.0", "minors to serve (latest patch each; fetched at start)") image := flag.String("image", "alpine:3.20", "base image") listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address") flag.Parse() b := &docker.Binaries{Root: binaries} tracked := strings.Split( versions, ",") if err := docker.RunUpdate(context.Background(), os.Stdout, docker.DefaultDiscovery(), b, tracked); err != nil { slog.Error("versions", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } rt, err := docker.New(docker.Config{Image: image, DataRoot: data, Binaries: b, Versions: docker.YAMLVersions{Tracked: tracked, Root: b.Root}}) if err != nil { slog.Error("docker", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) defer stop() h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{rt}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: listen}} if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil { slog.Error("host", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } }

title: Docker
heading: How it works
text: Each instance folder is mounted at /home/pockethost and the binary read-only at /home/pockethost/pocketbase . The container runs ./pocketbase serve --http 0.0.0.0:8090 , plus --dev for dev instances and --encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY when the instance has an encryption key. Its secrets are its environment. The port is published on 127.0.0.1 and the host proxies to it. This is the layout PocketHost's Node edge uses, so its instance folders and binary cache move as they are. Every container carries labels: p1.runtime , p1.instance , p1.version (the resolved release, such as pb:0.36.9 ) and p1.spec (a hash of its configuration, used to tell when it must restart). adopt_image also adopts unlabeled containers of an image, for taking over from another manager. Docker is reached over its socket API directly; there's no Docker SDK dependency.

title: Docker
heading: Status
text: Tested against a real Docker daemon, with upstream PocketBase 0.23 and PocketOne 0.0.1 side by side, alone and as a host's runtime. Not yet in production. go test ./... runs the Docker tests when a daemon is reachable (they're skipped with -short ). The first run downloads an upstream release and a PocketOne release into the user cache.
