title: Coding agents
text: Coding agents tend to write PocketPages as if it were a Node framework, or as if it were the 0.x npm package. The pocketpages Agent Skill teaches them v1: pb_pages/ , ctx , routing, templates, layouts, auth and deploying. It's built from these docs and the v1 spec, so it changes when they change. Claude Code /plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone /plugin install pocketone@pocketone The plugin also has the pocketone skill, for the binary, pocketone.yaml and its extensions. Other agents that read Agent Skills (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) npx skills add pockethost/pocketone Or copy agent/skills/pocketpages into your project.

title: Coding agents
heading: llms.txt
text: pocketone.dev/llms.txt indexes every docs page, these PocketPages pages included, with a one-line summary. pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt holds every docs page in one Markdown file.

title: API Routes and JSON
text: A +api.js file serves its folder's URL without a template. Use it for JSON, feeds, webhooks and anything else that isn't an HTML page. // pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20) return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) = ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') }))) }, } A request to /feeds/latest returns: [{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: How it works
text: +api.js has the same exports as +page.js : load , get , post , put , patch , delete . There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a 500 . [param] folders work as for pages: products/[id]/+api.js serves /products/123 . A folder can't have both a +api.js and an index page. Middleware runs for API routes too. ctx.httpError() thrown in a +api.js answers with JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "..." } .

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: Sending responses
text: ctx.res.json(data) / ctx.res.json(status, data) JSON ctx.res.text(text) / ctx.res.text(status, text) Plain text ctx.res.html(html) / ctx.res.html(status, html) HTML as-is, without layouts ctx.res.file(path) A file from pb_pages ctx.res.redirect(location) A redirect ctx.res.sse() A text/event-stream See res.

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: JSON from a page
text: JSON is only sent through ctx.res.json (or a +api.js ). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's +page.js can still answer with JSON for one method: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') }) }, }

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: Keep /api/ free
text: /api/ belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup. Put your routes somewhere else, such as feeds/ , xapi/ or hooks/ .

title: Asset Management
text: Static files in pb_pages (images, CSS, JS, fonts) can be served with fingerprinted URLs that change when the file changes.

title: Asset Management
heading: Where to put assets
text: Anywhere in pb_pages , next to the pages that use them or in a shared folder: pb_pages/ assets/ app.css logo.png feature/ index.md header.jpg

title: Asset Management
heading: In templates
text: Use asset() (the same as ctx.asset() ): " " asset('/assets/app.css') returns something like /assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css . Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged.

title: Asset Management
heading: In Markdown
text: Relative image paths go through asset() automatically: Header

title: Asset Management
heading: How it works
text: A fingerprinted name carries the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext . Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable . When the file changes, its hash and URL change, so browsers and CDNs fetch the new one. See asset and Caching.

title: Authentication
text: PocketPages keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie with the built-in auth plugin. Turn it on: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth'], }

title: Authentication
heading: How a request is authenticated
text: If the request has PocketBase's own Authorization header, ctx.auth is that record. Otherwise, the auth plugin reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token and sets ctx.auth (or clears a bad cookie). With neither, ctx.auth is null . Every ctx.session sign-in method sets the cookie, sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request, and returns { token, record } . ctx.session.signOut() clears it.

title: Authentication
heading: Protecting pages
text: // pb_pages/account/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() } Welcome, Log out Log in

title: Authentication
heading: Passwords
text: // pb_pages/login/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message, email } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } Email " / Password Log in

title: Authentication
heading: Registration
text: // pb_pages/register/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password, name } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.register(email, password, { data: { name } }) } catch (e) { return { error: Error registering: ${e.message} } } return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Welcome!' }) }, }

title: Authentication
heading: One-time passwords
text: A two-step form: request a code, then sign in with it. Turn on OTP for the collection in the dashboard and set up mail (Settings Mail settings). // pb_pages/login/otp/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { step, email, otpId, code } = ctx.req.body() try { if (step === 'request') { return { otpId: ctx.session.requestOTP(email), email } } ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code) return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Signed in' }) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message, otpId, email } } }, } Send code Check your email for the code. " / Sign in

title: Authentication
heading: OAuth2
text: Configure the provider in the dashboard (Collections users Options OAuth2). Then start the flow from a form: Sign in with Google // pb_pages/auth/oauth/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider) }, } requestOAuth2 stores its state in a cookie and redirects to the provider. The provider sends the user back to /auth/oauth/confirm (change it with { redirectPath } ): // pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { try { ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code')) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } See the Google OAuth2 speedrun for setting up Google.

title: Authentication
heading: Anonymous sign-in
text: // pb_pages/try/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signInAnonymously() return ctx.res.redirect('/dashboard') }, }

title: Authentication
heading: Your own auth flow
text: If you authenticate a record yourself, set the session cookie with ctx.session.signIn(record) .

title: Authentication
heading: Signing out
text: // pb_pages/logout/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, }

title: Authentication
heading: Security
text: Serve over HTTPS in production. Turn on PocketBase's rate limiting. Turn on email verification for your auth collection.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Fingerprinted assets
text: asset() adds a content hash to a file's URL: " The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256. Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable , so browsers and CDNs keep them for a year. When the file changes, the hash changes, and so does the URL. Old copies are never served for the new URL. A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged (and not fingerprinted).

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Static files
text: Every static file gets an ETag from its content hash. A request with a matching If-None-Match gets 304 Not Modified .

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Templates
text: A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. Edit a file and the next request uses the new version, in every mode.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Routes
text: The route table is built at startup and rebuilt whenever anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Pages
text: Rendered pages aren't cached. To let browsers or a CDN cache a page, set a header in a handler or middleware: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.res.header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=60') return next() }

title: Configuration with +config.js
text: Create pb_pages/+config.js to configure PocketPages for the app. It's only allowed at the top of pb_pages ; a +config.js in a subfolder is an error at startup. // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, }

title: Configuration with +config.js
heading: Options
text: plugins [] Built-in plugins by name, or JS plugin factories. EJS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. +config.js must export an object; exporting a function (0.x's (api) = ({...}) form) is an error. +config.js runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

title: Configuration with +config.js
heading: Plugins
text: Each entry in plugins is one of: A name , loaded with require : a _private/ file ( 'datastar' for the Datastar add-on), then a package in node_modules , then a built-in ( 'auth' or 'realtime' ). It must export a plugin factory. See Plugins. A JS plugin factory : a function that returns hooks, such as require('./_private/my-plugin.js') . A require with a path loads exactly that file, skipping the name lookup, so it's how you choose one copy over another. An object with a factory and options : { factory, ...options } . The object is passed to the factory as its config . module.exports = { plugins: [ 'auth', 'realtime', { factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Hello' }, ], } Plugin hooks run in the order the plugins are listed. See Plugin Authoring.

title: Configuration with +config.js
heading: Debug
text: debug: true turns on what dev mode ( --dev ) turns on: detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output. See Debugging.

title: Creating a PocketPages Page
text: A page is a template file, .ejs or .md , anywhere in pb_pages/ . Its path becomes its URL.

title: Creating a PocketPages Page
heading: Creating pages
text: Create a file : inside pb_pages/ , create an .ejs file. For example, an "About" page: pb_pages/about.ejs - serves "/about" index files : index maps to its folder. pb_pages/index.ejs - serves "/" pb_pages/products/index.ejs - serves "/products" (and "/products/") Nested pages : folders become URL segments. pb_pages/ ├── index.ejs - "/" ├── about.ejs - "/about" ├── contact.ejs - "/contact" └── products/ ├── index.ejs - "/products" └── details.ejs - "/products/details" Markdown pages : a .md file works the same way. It runs through EJS first, then Markdown. See Markdown. pb_pages/docs/routing.md - "/docs/routing" The extension is always dropped from the URL. To add data or handle forms, put a +page.js next to the page; see Loading Data.

title: ctx.app
text: The app ( $app ): records, collections, settings. Page code calls it directly, with no HTTP round trip. module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { product: ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id), latest: ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 10), } }, } Everything in PocketBase's JavaScript records and database docs that uses $app works on ctx.app . Calls through ctx.app don't apply collection API rules: page code is trusted server code. Check ctx.auth yourself before reading or changing data on a user's behalf.

title: ctx.asset
text: Returns the URL for a static file in pb_pages , with its content hash. In templates it's also available as asset . " Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged. The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext . Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable . Relative image paths in Markdown pages go through ctx.asset automatically. See Asset Management.

title: ctx.auth
text: The authenticated record, or null . It's set by: PocketBase's own auth, when the request has an Authorization header; the auth plugin, from its pb_auth cookie. Welcome, Please verify your email. Log in ctx.auth is a PocketBase record, so the usual record methods work: get(field) , getString(field) , email() , verified() , isSuperuser() , collection() .

title: ctx.auth
heading: Protecting pages
text: // pb_pages/account/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() }

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.data
text: A plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. It starts as {} . In templates it's also available as data . // +middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.user = ctx.auth return next() } // +page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') } // Object.assign'd into ctx.data }, } A handler's returned object is shallow-assigned into ctx.data . There is no deep merge.

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.params
text: Route parameters from [name] segments, as strings. Never includes query parameters (use ctx.req.query() ). In templates it's also available as params . /

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.route
text: { path, name, file } : the route pattern, the page name and its file relative to pb_pages . products/[id].ejs /products/[id] [id] docs/index.md /docs index A +page.js applies to every page in its folder; use ctx.route.name to tell them apart.

title: ctx.env
text: Returns an environment variable, or '' if it's unset. const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') It reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment. See Managing Secrets.

title: ctx.flash
text: A flash is a one-time message that survives one redirect, such as "Saved" after a form post.

title: ctx.flash
heading: Setting a flash
text: return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) The message is stored as JSON in a cookie ( pp_flash , HttpOnly , Max-Age=300 ). It can be any JSON value: return ctx.res.redirect('/cart', { flash: { type: 'success', text: 'Added to cart' } })

title: ctx.flash
heading: Reading it
text: On the next request, ctx.flash() returns the message and clears the cookie. It returns undefined when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value. " Read it in your layout to show flashes on every page.

title: The ctx Object
text: PocketPages creates one ctx object per request and passes it to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins. // +middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = next() // +page.js / +api.js module.exports = { load(ctx) {} } In templates, data , params , asset and meta are shortcuts for ctx.data , ctx.params , ctx.asset and ctx.meta .

title: The ctx Object
heading: Members
text: ctx.req The request: method, URL, query, headers, cookies, body, files ctx.res The response: status, headers, cookies, redirects, JSON, HTML, text, files, SSE ctx.data Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates ctx.params Route parameters ctx.route The matched route: { path, name, file } ctx.flash() The one-time message from the previous redirect ctx.auth The authenticated record, or null ctx.app The app ( $app ) ctx.pb() A JS SDK client acting as the visitor (API rules apply) ctx.env(name) Environment variable ctx.log debug , info , warn , error ctx.meta(key, value?) Per-request page metadata ctx.asset(path) Fingerprinted URL for a static file ctx.include(name, locals?) Render a _private/ partial from JS and get its text (same lookup as include , from the route's folder) ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?) Load a module from _private/ ctx.store(name, value?) The app's in-memory store ctx.pagesDir Absolute path of the app's pb_pages folder (read-only), e.g. for $os.readDir ctx.dev true in dev mode ctx.httpError(status, message) An error to throw for a specific status ctx.error { status, message } , in +error.ejs

title: The ctx Object
heading: Added by plugins
text: ctx.session auth ctx.realtime realtime ctx.datastar datastar JS plugins can add their own members with extendContext .

title: ctx.log
text: Writes to the app's log. ctx.log.debug('cart', ctx.data.cart) ctx.log.info('order placed') ctx.log.warn('stock is low') ctx.log.error('payment failed') debug only shows in dev mode ( --dev ) or with debug: true in +config.js . See Debugging.

title: ctx.meta
text: A per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. In templates it's also available as meta . " Layouts render after the page, so they see what the page set.

title: ctx.meta
heading: Front matter
text: In a .md page, each top-level key of the YAML front matter is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) : title: About us description: Who we are

title: ctx.pb() (JS SDK)
text: ctx.pb() returns a PocketBase JS SDK client, the same API you use in the browser: // pb_pages/posts/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { const page = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getList(1, 20, { filter: 'published = true', sort: '-created', expand: 'author', }) return { posts: page.items } }, } It acts as the visitor. When someone is signed in ( ctx.auth , for example through the auth plugin), the client is authenticated as them; otherwise it's a guest. Your collections' API rules, expand and hidden fields apply exactly as they would in the browser. It's synchronous. Calls return their result directly; no await . No network. Requests go straight to your app's own API, in-process. There's no host or port to set, and it works the same on any server. Errors throw the SDK's ClientResponseError : try { const post = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getOne(ctx.params.id) } catch (e) { if (e.status === 404) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such post') throw e } Limits: only /api/ routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported, so use ctx.app for those.

title: ctx.pb() (JS SDK)
heading: ctx.pb() or ctx.app?
text: Permissions the visitor's: API rules apply full access, no rules API the JS SDK, same as the browser PocketBase's JSVM API ( findRecordsByFilter , save , ...) Use it for reading and writing on the visitor's behalf admin work, background jobs, anything rules shouldn't limit When in doubt, use ctx.pb() : if a page shows something, the visitor is allowed to see it.

title: ctx.req
text: method "GET" , "POST" , ... url { href, origin, pathname, search } query(name) First value of a query parameter as a string, or undefined query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter header(name) Request header, '' if absent cookie(name) Cookie value as a string, or undefined cookie(name, { json: true }) Cookie parsed as JSON ( undefined if absent or not JSON) cookies() { name: value } , strings body() Parsed body: a JSON object, or form fields as { name: value } (repeated names as arrays) files(name) Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase filesystem.File values ready for a record field ip Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) event The underlying PocketBase RequestEvent , for anything not covered here Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

title: ctx.req
heading: Examples
text: You asked for Page Browser:

title: ctx.req
heading: Forms
text: body() parses JSON, application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data : // pb_pages/contact/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, message } = ctx.req.body() // ... }, }

title: ctx.req
heading: File uploads
text: Upload module.exports = { post(ctx) { const record = ctx.app.findRecordById('users', ctx.auth.id) record.set('avatar', ctx.req.files('avatar')[0]) ctx.app.save(record) return ctx.res.redirect('/account') }, }

title: ctx.req
heading: Cookies
text: const theme = ctx.req.cookie('theme') // 'dark' or undefined const prefs = ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) ?? {} Set cookies with ctx.res.cookie() .

title: ctx.res
text: status(code) Status for the rendered page. Returns ctx.res . header(name, value) Set a response header. header(name) reads it back. cookie(name, value, options?) Set a cookie. clearCookie(name, options?) Expire a cookie (same path / domain as when set). redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?) or redirect(location, status) Send a redirect. status must be a 3xx code. flash sets a one-time message. json(data) / json(status, data) Send JSON. html(html) / html(status, html) Send HTML as-is (no layouts). text(text) / text(status, text) Send plain text. file(path) Send a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages ). sse() Start a text/event-stream response. layout(false) Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). Returns ctx.res . sent true once a response has been sent. Once a response is sent, the later steps of the request (handlers, template, layouts) are skipped.

title: ctx.res
heading: Status and headers
text: Not here

title: ctx.res
heading: Redirects
text: return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) return ctx.res.redirect('/new-home', 301) // or { status: 301 }

title: ctx.res
heading: Cookies
text: ctx.res.cookie('theme', 'dark', { maxAge: 60 60 24 365 }) ctx.res.cookie('prefs', { compact: true }) // objects are JSON.stringify'd ctx.res.clearCookie('theme') Non-string values are JSON.stringify 'd. The value is then percent-encoded ( encodeURIComponent ), and ctx.req.cookie decodes it. Defaults: path=/ , HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , and Secure when the request is HTTPS. Options: path , domain , maxAge (seconds), expires (a Date , milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with maxAge too, browsers use maxAge ), httpOnly , secure , sameSite .

title: ctx.res
heading: JSON, HTML, text and files
text: return ctx.res.json({ ok: true }) return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id }) return ctx.res.html(' Fragment ') return ctx.res.text(404, 'Not found') return ctx.res.file('downloads/manual.pdf')

title: ctx.res
heading: Server-sent events
text: sse() starts a text/event-stream response and returns { send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() } : // pb_pages/clock/+api.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { const stream = ctx.res.sse() stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString()) stream.close() }, } Streaming is only available through sse() . Templates return their text all at once.

title: ctx.resolve
text: Loads a module from a _private/ folder. The lookup starts at the route's folder (the page being served), wherever ctx.resolve is called from, so a layout or partial gets the same answer as the page: _private/ in the route's folder, then each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ . Without an extension, the name, then .js , .ts and .json are tried. // pb_pages/_private/shout.js module.exports = (s) = String(s).toUpperCase()

title: ctx.resolve
heading: Modes
text: require (default) The module's exports raw The file's text script The text wrapped in style The text wrapped in

title: ctx.resolve
heading: Modules from node_modules
text: Page code can also require() by name: _private/ folders first (nearest to the file calling require ), then packages from pb_pages/node_modules , then the app's usual module paths. See JavaScript Runtime.

title: ctx.store
text: The app's in-memory store ( $app.store() ). Set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.store('visits', (ctx.store('visits') 0) + 1) Visits since start: Values are shared by every request to the app. The store lives in memory: it's empty again after the app restarts. Keep anything that must last in a collection.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Dev mode
text: Run pocketone with --dev : pocketone serve --dev Dev mode turns on: detailed error pages (message, file and line, trimmed stack; see Errors); ctx.log.debug output.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: debug: true
text: To get the same in production, set debug: true in +config.js : module.exports = { debug: true, } Turn it off again when you're done. Detailed error pages show error messages, file paths and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Logging
text: ctx.log writes to the app's log: ctx.log.debug('loaded product', ctx.params.id) // only in dev mode or with debug: true ctx.log.info('order placed') ctx.log.warn('stock is low') ctx.log.error('payment failed') See log.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Template changes
text: Templates are cached by content hash and the route table is rebuilt on any file change, in every mode. If a change doesn't show, check the app's log for a startup error (bad file name, route conflict): the previous route table keeps serving until the error is fixed.

title: Going Live
text: A PocketPages app is a pb_pages folder. To go live, run PocketOne on your server (pages is built in) and put pb_pages next to pb_data , along with your other pb_ folders: pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ Or point pocketone at it with --pagesDir .

title: Going Live
heading: Updating
text: Copy the changed files into pb_pages . The route table is rebuilt on any change, and templates are cached by content hash, so updates show on the next request without restarting the app. If an update has a startup error (a bad name or a route conflict), it's logged with the file path and the previous route table keeps serving.

title: Going Live
heading: Before you go live
text: Run without --dev , and keep debug: false in +config.js . Set secrets as environment variables (see Managing Secrets). Serve over HTTPS. Cookies set with ctx.res.cookie are marked Secure on HTTPS requests.

title: Going Live
heading: Multitenant hosts
text: Under a multitenant PocketOne host, every instance has its own pb_pages , and page code runs with the same limits as the rest of the instance's JS.

title: Directory Structure
text: All pages live in the pb_pages/ folder, next to pb_data/ : myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ +config.js +layout.ejs index.ejs about.ejs _private/ nav.ejs assets/ app.css products/ [id]/ +page.js index.ejs

title: Directory Structure
heading: Special names
text: A file or folder name starting with one of these characters is never a URL: + Framework file: +layout.ejs (or .jsx , .tsx ), +middleware.js , +page.js , +api.js , one of each per folder. +config.js , +error.ejs and +404.ejs are allowed only at the top of pb_pages . Any other + name, any other extension (such as +layout.md ), and a top-only file in a subfolder are errors at startup. _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules for include() and ctx.resolve() . Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes). . Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level .well-known/ , which is served as static files (ACME challenges, security.txt , app links). node_modules/ is never routed either.

title: Directory Structure
heading: Groups
text: A folder named (name) groups files without adding a URL segment: (marketing)/pricing.ejs serves /pricing . A group can have its own +layout.ejs , +middleware.js and _private/ .

title: Directory Structure
heading: What else
text: Every other file is a static file, served as-is. Page code can require() modules by name from _private/ folders (nearest first), then pb_pages/node_modules , then pb_hooks/node_modules and the app folder's node_modules , then the app's usual module paths. Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves pb_pages . A pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup, because /api/ belongs to PocketBase.

title: EJS
text: EJS is always on. There is nothing to install or configure.

title: EJS
heading: Tags
text: Run JS, no output Output, HTML-escaped Output, raw Nothing Also remove the newline right after the tag Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line ' % code Same as

title: EJS
heading: Escaping
text: replaces & " ' with & < > " ' . null and undefined output as an empty string. "x" ' % raw ' % Use <%- only for HTML you trust, such as the output of include() or slot() .

title: EJS
heading: In scope
text: Inside a template you can use: ctx The request context data ctx.data params ctx.params include Render a partial slot Define or read a slot asset ctx.asset meta ctx.meta require Load a module: a path, or a name looked up in _private/ then node_modules (see JavaScript Runtime)

title: EJS
heading: Output
text: A template returns its text. There is no echo() ; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

title: EJS
heading: Caching
text: A template is compiled once per content hash and reused, so an edited file is recompiled on the next request.

title: Errors
heading: Thrown errors
text: Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a 500 . Dev mode or debug: true : an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the .ejs or .md source), and the stack trimmed to pb_pages -relative paths. Otherwise: a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log.

title: Errors
heading: ctx.httpError(status, message)
text: Throw ctx.httpError() to answer with a specific status: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { let product try { product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByData('products', 'slug', ctx.params.id) } catch (e) { throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product') // findFirstRecordByData throws when nothing matches } ctx.data.product = product }, } In a page, it sends that status with a plain page showing message . In a +api.js , it sends JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "No such product" } .

title: Errors
heading: A custom error page
text: Create pb_pages/+error.ejs . It renders for every ctx.httpError and for every 500 outside dev mode, inside the root layout, with ctx.error = { status, message } : { % Error +error and +404 live only at the top of pb_pages . Either may be .ejs , .jsx or .tsx .

title: Errors
heading: A custom 404 page
text: Create pb_pages/+404.ejs . It renders inside the root layout, with status 404 , for a GET or HEAD that nothing answers: no page, no file in pb_public and no PocketBase route. It never renders for /api/ or /_/ . The root +middleware.js runs first, and page code can still change the status. { % Not found Not found Nothing lives at .

title: Pages
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder, next to your pb_data . Each file becomes a route: EJS, Markdown, JSX and TSX templates, layouts, middleware and API routes, plus static files. Page code runs in your app's JS VM, so it can use your data directly. This is PocketPages v1, formerly the npm PocketPages package. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Pages
heading: Install
text: Pages is built into pocketone and on whenever a pb_pages folder exists next to pb_data . There's no switch: no folder, no pages. If the folder appears while the app runs, it starts serving it. In your own Go build, register it after the JS VM (ext/jsvm), since page code runs there: app := pocketbase.New() jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) // serves pb_pages next to pb_data pages.RegisterCommand(app.RootCmd) // the pages create and pages starters commands app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages . See example/main.go and Create your own extension.

title: Pages
heading: Where the folder is
text: By default the folder is pb_pages next to pb_data . To use another one: pocketone serve --pagesDir /path/to/pb_pages A relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir . Pages has no pocketone.yaml section.

title: Pages
heading: +config.js
text: Settings for your pages live in the folder itself, in pb_pages/+config.js : module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, } plugins [] Module names (a _private/ file, a node_modules package or a path, loaded with require ), built-in plugins by name ( auth , realtime , used when no module by that name is found), or JS plugins such as the add-ons. EJS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. +config.js runs on each page request. Unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error, and the reason goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Dev mode
text: When the app runs in dev mode ( --dev , or app.dev in pocketone.yaml ), or +config.js sets debug: true , you get detailed error pages with the file and line, and ctx.log.debug output. Otherwise visitors see a plain "Something went wrong" page and the full error goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Start from a starter kit
text: pocketone pages starters # list the kits pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs cd myapp pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. pages create makes a new folder (it must not exist yet) with pb_pages and anything the kit needs beside it, such as pb_migrations . Without --starter you get minimal . minimal One page, no layout, no build step (the default). mvp One page styled with MVP.css. htmx A realtime chat and counter with htmx and the realtime plugin. daisyui A navbar and drawer layout with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. daisyui-docs A docs site from Markdown pages. datastar A realtime chat with rooms, with Datastar. auth Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous), email flows and a protected account page.

title: Pages
heading: Write pages
text: Add or edit files in pb_pages and reload the browser; no restart is needed. A few examples of what the folder holds: pb_pages/ +config.js settings (above) +layout.ejs wraps every page +error.ejs your error page index.ejs / about.md /about blog/[slug].ejs /blog/anything feeds/rss/+api.js /feeds/rss, a route without a template _private/ partials, never served assets/app.css a static file The full contract is in SPEC.md: routes and precedence, middleware, +page.js and +api.js , EJS, partials, slots and layouts, Markdown, JSX and TSX, the ctx object, errors, the built-in auth and realtime plugins, JS plugins, add-ons and the changes from 0.x. Highlights: Static files get ETags and fingerprinted URLs through asset() . ctx.pb() is the bundled PocketBase JS SDK, called in-process as the visitor. ctx.res.sse() streams server-sent events. The auth plugin gives cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: password, OTP, anonymous, register, OAuth2 and the email flows (verification, password reset, email change). Accounts that need MFA (the collection's MFA is on and its rule matches) are refused by every pages sign-in method; pages has no second sign-in step yet.

title: Pages
heading: What you'll see in the log
text: Problems in the folder (a bad file name, two files claiming the same route) are logged as pages: ... errors. If the site served cleanly before, pages keeps the previous routes until the folder builds cleanly again. Errors thrown by page code are logged in full.

title: Pages
heading: Try the demo
text: example/ is a demo app with EJS, Markdown, JSX, auth, ctx.pb() , SSE and a JSON route. It has a live speed check at /speed . cd example && go run . serve --dir=./pb_data

title: Pages
heading: Works with
text: Pocker Pages is in the standard set, so every instance serves its own pb_pages (below). Cache Compiled templates and modules go in the pages.compiled bucket (cache/v1, at most 32 MiB per app), keyed by content, so old versions are evicted instead of piling up. On a multisite host, instances serving the same files share one compiled copy. On a multisite host they also outlive an instance's restarts, since the cache belongs to the host. With the cache off, each JS VM compiles a file the first time it meets it. Deploy pb_pages deploys with your other pb_ folders. pull doesn't fetch it by default; name it: pocketone pull prod pb_pages .

title: Pages
heading: Under pocker
text: Pages is a member of the standard set, so every instance serves its own /pb_pages , in the stock pocketone binary and in any host built on standard.New() . A host without the standard set adds it like any extension: srv := &pocker.Server{Config: cfg, Extensions: []pocker.Extension{pages.New(pages.Config{})}} Each start of an instance's app gets its own route table, compiled templates (in its own pages.compiled bucket; identical files share one copy in the host's cache) and caches. An instance that sleeps drops them; nothing is shared between instances. Page code runs in the instance's own sandboxed JS VM (jsvm), under its limits (execution time, memory, stack). include , require , ctx.resolve , ctx.res.file and asset never reach outside the instance's pb_pages ; $os file access stays inside the instance folder. Tests: multiinstance_test.go. An instance turns pages off in its settings with extensions: { pages: { enabled: false } } . Measured on the earlier goja engine (same machine as Speed, docs kit; not yet re-measured on jsvm): each awake instance added about 2.3 MB (50 instances: 41 MB idle to 155 MB), and one instance under pocker served about 4,000 requests/s (p50 5.6 ms, p99 80 ms at 50 concurrent). To try it: copy sites into multiinstance/example/pb_root/ .localhost/pb_pages , run go run ./multiinstance/example , and open http:// .localhost:8791 .

title: Pages
heading: Building on pages
text: Read the routes. pages.For(app) returns the service: Dir() is the folder, Table() the current route table, Errors() the problems from the last build. JS plugins. A factory in +config.js can add to ctx , run on each request and transform rendered HTML (SPEC.md, section 9.2). Add-ons are built this way.

title: Pages
heading: Example
text: example/main.go serves the demo in example/pb_pages : EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth, SSE and a JSON route. Run go run . serve --dir=./pb_data in example/ and open http://127.0.0.1:8090. // Command example runs one PocketOne app that serves the demo in ./pb_pages (EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth, // ctx.pb(), SSE, a JSON route, +404). ./pb_migrations creates a "notes" collection // with three seed notes. From this folder: // // go run . serve --dir=./pb_data // // Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. Edit anything in pb_pages and reload; no restart needed. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / // password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Pages
heading: Speed
text: ext/pages against npm PocketPages 0.22.5 (the last 0.x release), serving the same starter kit pages: the 0.x kits in pb_hooks/pages on stock PocketBase 0.41.1, the v1 ports in pb_pages on the PocketOne binary. minimal / (EJS) npm 0.22.5 620 30 ms 670 ms 5.7 ms ext/pages 10,850 1.8 ms 37 ms 0.2 ms daisyui-docs /docs/overview (layouts, Markdown, partial) npm 0.22.5 580 28 ms 1.1 s 6.5 ms ext/pages 6,510 4.1 ms 49 ms 0.4 ms PocketBase's own /api/health (the ceiling) PocketOne 55,000 0.9 ms 2.4 ms 0.1 ms About 17.5× more requests per second on the simple page and 11× on the docs page, with p99 latency 20× lower. Single requests take 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. Memory after each run was similar (170 to 350 MB for both). Why: 0.x parsed routes, ran EJS through a JS implementation and loaded its plugins inside the JS VM on every request. v1 builds the route table once, compiles each template once (EJS to JS in Go, Markdown with goldmark) and enters the JS VM once per request. How it was measured (2026-11-11): Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, macOS 27, Go 1.27.4, hey against 127.0.0.1 . Each server was warmed with 500 requests, then hey -z 10s -c 50 and hey -n 2000 -c 1 ; two rounds, which agreed within 5%. Every response was a 200 with the full page. The 0.x docs kit inlines about 6 KB of CSS into each page where v1 links app.css . Rerun it with bench/run.sh : cp -R starters/daisyui-docs /tmp/v1-docs pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password --dir=/tmp/v1-docs/pb_data bench/run.sh v1-docs 8804 /docs/overview "$(which pocketone)" /tmp/v1-docs

title: HTMX Integration
text: HTMX lets HTML elements fetch HTML from the server and swap it into the page. PocketPages renders that HTML.

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Setting up HTMX
text: Add HTMX to your layout:

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Route organization
text: HTMX requests want HTML fragments, not whole pages wrapped in your layout. Put the layout in a group, and the fragment routes outside it: pb_pages/ (site)/ # Pages with layouts +layout.ejs # Main site layout index.ejs # / products/ index.ejs # /products xapi/ # HTMX endpoints (no layouts) products/ search.ejs # /xapi/products/search create/ +page.js index.ejs # /xapi/products/create (site) holds full pages. Its +layout.ejs wraps them, and the group adds nothing to the URL. xapi/ holds fragments. No layout applies to them, because there is no +layout.ejs at the root. Don't name the folder api/ : /api/ belongs to PocketBase. A handler can also send a fragment directly with ctx.res.html() , which never applies layouts.

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Sharing partials
text: Render the same fragment on the first page load and in HTMX responses by keeping it in a _private/ partial: pb_pages/ _private/ product-card.ejs # shared partial (site)/ products/ index.ejs # includes the partial xapi/ products/ more.ejs # includes the same partial " Load More

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Forms
text: Create Product // pb_pages/xapi/products/create/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { name, description } = ctx.req.body() const product = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('products')) product.set('name', name) product.set('description', description) ctx.app.save(product) return { product } }, }

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Out-of-band updates
text: Update more than one element with a single response: Products

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Realtime updates
text: With the realtime plugin, a page can push rendered HTML to every subscriber. A template has include() , so render the partial there and send it: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] } // pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.js module.exports = { post() {}, // accept POST; the page below does the work } Send In the browser, subscribe to the topic with the PocketBase JS SDK and append what arrives: const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin) pb.realtime.subscribe('chat', (html) = { document.getElementById('chat').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html) })

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Best practices
text: Route organization : keep fragment routes outside the layout group, in a folder like xapi/ . Response size : return only the HTML the swap needs. Loading states : use hx-indicator to show progress. Security : check ctx.auth in middleware before changing data, validate input on the server, and debounce triggers like search inputs.

title: Installation
text: PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne as the pages extension ( ext/pages ). There is nothing to install from npm: the standard pocketone binary includes it. pocketone pages create myapp creates a new app. Add --starter to start from a starter kit. _Note: --dir tells pocketone where pb_data is. PocketPages looks for pb_pages next to it. Create the superuser before the first serve ; otherwise PocketBase opens its superuser installer in your browser._ Browse to http://localhost:8090 and you'll see the starter's home page. The default minimal kit is one splash page: PocketPages }) % To start editing, open myapp/pb_pages/index.ejs Changes appear on the next refresh. The app doesn't restart.

title: Installation
heading: Where pages live
text: Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others: myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ PocketPages finds the folder at pb_pages next to pb_data , or wherever --pagesDir points. If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app. Under a multitenant host, every instance has its own pb_pages .

title: Installation
heading: How does it work?
text: PocketPages is a multi-page app server for PocketOne. It listens for requests and renders pages using file-based routing rules, like old-school PHP. URLs under /api/ and /_/ always belong to PocketBase. A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase.

title: JavaScript Runtime
text: Middleware, handlers, templates and plugins run in PocketBase's JavaScript runtime. It is neither a browser nor Node.js, so there are no Web APIs or Node APIs such as Buffer and require('fs') . Each request runs as one unit under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory). Under a multitenant host, that's the instance's sandbox.

title: JavaScript Runtime
heading: Talking to the app
text: Use ctx.app , which is $app . PocketBase's JS docs cover database operations and record operations: const records = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter( 'articles', 'status = {:status} && author = {:author}', '-created', 20, 0, { status: 'pending', author: ctx.auth.id } )

title: JavaScript Runtime
heading: Can I use my favorite npm package?
text: Maybe. Page code can require() modules by name from _private/ folders (nearest first), then from pb_pages/node_modules , then pb_hooks/node_modules and the app folder's node_modules , then from the app's usual module paths. A _private/ file with the same name as a package wins. Packages that are plain CommonJS JavaScript, with no Node or browser APIs, have the best chance of working. Install packages in the app folder (next to pb_pages ), not inside pb_pages . Every file in pb_pages that isn't private is served, so a package.json there would be public: cd myapp npm install some-package const somePackage = require('some-package') Your own modules go in _private/ and load with ctx.resolve() .

title: JSX and TSX
text: A .jsx or .tsx file is a template, just like an .ejs file. It can be a page, a layout ( +layout.tsx ), an error page ( +error.tsx , +404.tsx ) or a partial in _private/ . PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no npm install , no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked. // pb_pages/products/[id].tsx import Price from './_private/Price' export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) { slot('title', data.product.getString('name')) return ( {data.product.getString('name')} ) } // pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) = ${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}

title: JSX and TSX
heading: Props
text: The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets: ctx The request context. data , params , meta The same as ctx.data , ctx.params and ctx.meta . asset , include The same helpers EJS templates have. include(name, locals) returns HTML you can put in JSX. slot slot(name) reads a named slot, slot(name, content) sets one, slot() is the inner content. children In a layout, the inner content. A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props. EJS can include a .jsx or .tsx partial the same way: its locals become props.

title: JSX and TSX
heading: Server-rendered HTML only
text: JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration and no client-side React. Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: onclick="..." , hx-get , data-on:click . Text and attribute values are escaped. dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} inserts raw HTML. class and className both work, as do for and htmlFor . style takes a string or an object: { marginTop: 4 } renders margin-top:4 . true renders a bare attribute. false , null and undefined leave it out. gets in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

title: JSX and TSX
heading: Layouts
text: // pb_pages/+layout.tsx export default function Layout({ children, slot }: any) { return ( {slot('title')} {children} ) } Layouts in .ejs , .jsx and .tsx mix freely: an EJS page can sit inside a TSX layout and the other way round.

title: JSX and TSX
heading: TypeScript modules
text: +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts and any .ts file reached by require or import work like their .js versions. A module whose only export is export default behaves like module.exports = ... . Components are ordinary modules, so import Card from './_private/Card' resolves the same way as require . When a partial name has no extension, .ejs , .md , .jsx and .tsx are tried, in that order.

title: Layouts and Slots
text: +layout.ejs files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every +layout from its own folder up to pb_pages/ , applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as +layout.ejs , +layout.jsx or +layout.tsx . A layout can't be Markdown: +layout.md is an error at startup. pb_pages/ +layout.ejs # applied last (outermost) products/ +layout.ejs # applied first [id].ejs For /products/123 , [id].ejs renders, then products/+layout.ejs wraps it, then +layout.ejs wraps that.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: slot()
text: In a layout, slot() returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout. My Application © My Application without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: Named slots
text: A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with slot(name, fn) . fn 's output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with slot(name) , which returns '' if it isn't defined. { % Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's fn , slot(name) still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it: { % Docs:

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: Data in layouts
text: Layouts render after the page, with the same ctx . Everything middleware, +page.js and the page put on ctx.data or ctx.meta is there.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: When layouts are skipped
text: When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another Content-Type ). When a handler or middleware sent the response itself ( ctx.res.json , ctx.res.html , ctx.res.redirect , ...). For +api.js routes, which have no template. After ctx.res.layout(false) , called from middleware, +page.js or the page itself. With the Datastar add-on, for requests that carry Datastar-Request: true . To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call ctx.res.layout(false) , put the layout in a group ( (site)/+layout.ejs ) and the fragments outside it, or send them with ctx.res.html() .

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
text: You can load data right in a template, or in a +page.js file next to it.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Inline data loading
text: The simplest way is a block at the top of your template: Products

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Server script blocks
text: For better formatting support in editors, you can write ' % instead of . They mean the same thing: ' % const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100) const categories = ctx.app.findAllRecords('categories') Products by Category

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Structured loading with +page.js
text: A +page.js file keeps data loading and form handling out of the template: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) }, post(ctx) { const { qty } = ctx.req.body() // ... return ctx.res.redirect( /products/${ctx.params.id} , { flash: 'Added to cart' }) }, }

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Exports
text: +page.js exports any of load , get , post , put , patch and delete . load runs first, for every method. Then the handler for the request method runs, if there is one. Then the page renders. A handler can set fields on ctx.data , or return a plain object. A returned object is shallow-assigned into ctx.data ( Object.assign ); there is no deep merge. module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') } }, get(ctx) { ctx.data.mode = 'view' }, } If a handler sends a response ( ctx.res.redirect , json , html , text , file , sse ), the page doesn't render.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: One +page.js per folder
text: A +page.js applies to every page in its folder. Use ctx.route.name to tell them apart: module.exports = { load(ctx) { if (ctx.route.name === 'details') { ctx.data.reviews = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('reviews', 'product = {:id}', '-created', 20, 0, { id: ctx.params.id }) } }, }

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Methods without a handler
text: Every handler is optional. A page renders for any method, like PHP, so a template can handle a form on its own: Thanks, ! Send A post (or put , ...) handler in +page.js is the tidier place for form logic as a page grows, but you don't need one. Only routes with nothing to render, +api.js and a +page.js without a page, answer 405 for a method they have no handler for.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Example: a contact form
text: // pb_pages/contact/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') } }, post(ctx) { const { email, message, department } = ctx.req.body() try { const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('messages')) record.set('email', email) record.set('message', message) record.set('department', department) ctx.app.save(record) } catch (e) { return { error: 'Failed to send message', values: { email, message, department } } } return ctx.res.redirect('/contact', { flash: 'Thanks, we got your message.' }) }, } " / " Send

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Pages without a template
text: A +page.js in a folder with no page file serves the folder's URL from JS. Use it for a page you'd rather build in code, or for a URL that only acts and redirects: // pb_pages/logout/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } // pb_pages/hello/+page.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { return ctx.res.html( Hello ${ctx.auth ? ctx.auth.getString('name') : 'there'} ) }, } With no template to render, each handler must send a response; returning without one is a 500. Methods without a handler answer 405 , GET included: /logout above only takes POST . Folder middleware runs; layouts don't, so wrap HTML yourself (or render a partial with ctx.include ). Errors show your +error.ejs page. For JSON responses and JSON errors, use +api.js instead.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Middleware or +page.js?
text: Only the route's own folder's +page.js runs. Every +middleware.js from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder runs, root first. Use middleware for data or checks that a whole section of the site shares.

title: Markdown Support
text: A .md file is a page, just like an .ejs file. Markdown is always on.

title: Markdown Support
heading: How it works
text: EJS first : the file runs through EJS, so every EJS tag works in Markdown. Then Markdown : the result is rendered as Markdown: CommonMark plus GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks.

title: Markdown Support
heading: Front matter
text: YAML between lines at the top of the file is front matter. Each top-level key is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) : title: My Blog Post description: A detailed guide about something interesting # Content starts here... Read the values in a layout with meta : "

title: Markdown Support
heading: Headings
text: Headings get id s, so you can link to them: the text is lowercased, characters other than a-z , 0-9 , - , _ and space are removed, and spaces become - . ## Front matter gets id="front-matter" .

title: Markdown Support
heading: Images
text: Relative image paths go through ctx.asset , so they get fingerprinted URLs: Logo

title: Markdown Support
heading: Markdown partials
text: A .md file in a _private/ folder can be included from EJS with include() . It's rendered the same way, EJS then Markdown:

title: Markdown Support
heading: Notes
text: Layouts are +layout.ejs , +layout.jsx or +layout.tsx . A layout can't be Markdown: +layout.md is an error at startup. A Markdown page is still wrapped by the layouts above it.

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
text: Middleware files ( +middleware.js ) run before your handlers and templates. Use them to: Check authentication Load data a whole section shares Set headers Validate requests

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Basic example
text: // pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') ctx.data.section = 'admin' return next() } One signature: (ctx, next) . Call next() to continue, and return its result. Returning without calling next() ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (a 500 ; in dev mode the error page names the middleware file). Share data through ctx.data .

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Order
text: Every +middleware.js from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder runs, root first. Groups count too. pb_pages/ +middleware.js # runs first (all routes) products/ +middleware.js # runs second (/products/...) [id]/ +middleware.js # runs third (/products/[id]) The full order for a request is: Plugins' onRequest Middleware, root first The folder's +page.js or +api.js ( load , then the method's handler) The template, then layouts, innermost first The response If any step sends a response, the later steps are skipped.

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Auth guard
text: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() }

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Request validation
text: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(ctx.params.id)) throw ctx.httpError(400, 'Invalid ID') return next() }

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Shared data
text: // pb_pages/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.categories = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('categories', 'active = true', 'name', 100) return next() } "

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Headers
text: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.res.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY') return next() }

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
text: PocketPages v1 is part of PocketOne (the pages extension). It keeps the ideas of the npm package (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for 0.x don't run unchanged. There is no migration tool. Start a new app with pocketone pages create , then move your pages over using the list below. The npm package is being retired.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Folder and boot
text: pb_hooks/pages/ , booted by require('pocketpages') in a .pb.js file pb_pages/ next to pb_data . No boot file, no npm install. create-pocketpages pocketone pages create [--starter ] Delete the .pb.js boot file and the pocketpages dependencies, and move the contents of pb_hooks/pages/ to pb_pages/ .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: The context object
text: 0.x passed an api object and spread its members into each template. v1 passes one ctx object with req , res , data , params , route and helpers. See the ctx reference. request , response ctx.req , ctx.res body() , formData ctx.req.body() redirect(path) ctx.res.redirect(path) response.redirect(path, status) ctx.res.redirect(path, status) (unchanged) env() , store() , dbg() , info() , warn() , error() ctx.env() , ctx.store() , ctx.log.debug() / info() / warn() / error() auth , request.auth ctx.auth resolve(name) ctx.resolve(name) Inside templates, data , params , asset and meta are still available without the ctx. prefix. The other 0.x template globals are gone, including resolve , redirect and env : use ctx.resolve() , ctx.res.redirect() and ctx.env() .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Parameters, query strings and cookies
text: Query parameters are no longer mixed into params , and nothing is JSON-parsed for you. ctx.params holds route parameters only; read the query string with ctx.req.query(name) , which returns strings. Cookies are strings. Pass { json: true } to parse one: ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Middleware
text: 0.x middleware either returned a value or called next(extra) , depending on how many arguments it declared. v1 has one signature: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.user = ctx.auth return next() } Put shared data on ctx.data . See Middleware.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Loaders
text: +load.js , +get.js , +post.js and friends are replaced by one +page.js per folder that exports load , get , post , put , patch and delete . Returned objects are shallow-assigned into ctx.data (no deep merge). As in 0.x, every handler is optional and a page renders for any method, so templates that check the request method keep working ( request.method becomes ctx.req.method ). // 0.x: +load.js module.exports = (api) = ({ products: $app.findAllRecords('products') }) // v1: +page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') } }, } See Loading Data.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: JSON
text: 0.x sent template output as JSON if it parsed as JSON. v1 never does. Send JSON with ctx.res.json() , usually from a +api.js file. See API Routes and JSON.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Layouts and slots
text: comments in the page slot('name', () = { % ...<% }) slot and slots.name in layouts slot() and slot('name') See Layouts and Slots.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Output
text: echo() is gone. A template returns its text; anything you want in the output goes through a tag. For streaming, use ctx.res.sse() .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Flash messages
text: 0.x put the message in a ?__flash= query parameter with redirect(path, { message }) . v1 uses a one-time cookie: return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) Read it on the next request with ctx.flash() . See flash.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Assets
text: asset() URLs now carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256, not the full hash.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Configuration and plugins
text: +config.js still takes plugin package names, which are loaded with require as before, but the packages must be v1 plugins: the 0.x pocketpages-plugin- packages don't run on v1. auth and realtime are built in, EJS and Markdown are always on, and Datastar is an add-on you copy into pb_pages/_private/ and list as 'datastar' . Its API is 0.x's, with signals() added alongside readSignals . npm plugin package names and EJS options are gone. +config.js must export an object ( module.exports = { ... } ). 0.x's function form, module.exports = (api) = ({ ... }) , is an error. A package.json at the app's root still works: bare require('pkg') looks in the app folder's node_modules after pb_pages . EJS and Markdown are always on. pocketpages-plugin-ejs and pocketpages-plugin-marked have no v1 equivalent because they aren't needed. The auth plugin no longer goes through the JS SDK over HTTP ( api.pb() ). Use ctx.session. , which calls the app directly. See Authentication. See +config.js and Plugins.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Behavior that changed quietly
text: These don't fail with an error, so check for them when porting: Cookies are HttpOnly by default. Pass { httpOnly: false } to ctx.res.cookie for a cookie your page's JS reads. The pb_auth cookie stays HttpOnly , so pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie) in the browser no longer works. Realtime messages are JSON-encoded. ctx.realtime.send(topic, data) sends JSON.stringify(data) , so a string (such as an HTML fragment) arrives in quotes: JSON.parse it on the client. A filter now gets one argument, the client, and only narrows clients already subscribed to the topic. .md , .jsx and .tsx files are always pages , never served as static files. Front matter is plain YAML. EJS tags inside it aren't run. require never leaves pb_pages . To load code from pb_hooks , use require(__hooks + '/lib/x') . Hook files ( .pb.js ) go in pb_hooks . In pb_pages they're an error and aren't served.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Removed globals
text: url() ctx.req.url stringify() JSON.stringify micro-dash plain JavaScript pb() (JS SDK plugin) ctx.pb() , built in: same SDK, no host setting, runs in-process as the signed-in user

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Routing
text: A route with fewer segments no longer matches a longer URL. Segment counts must match: products/[id].ejs serves /products/123 but not /products/123/reviews .

title: Overview of PocketPages
text: PocketPages turns a folder of files into a server-rendered website, inside PocketOne. It is built in as the pages extension ( ext/pages ): no npm package, no boot file, no build step. Use PocketPages to create slim and modern web apps: Start small and iterate SEO-first principles No build step Fast server-side rendering

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Hello world in just one file
text: Inside you write plain JavaScript. Every page gets a ctx object with the request, the response, your data, and the app itself ( ctx.app ), so you can read and write records directly.

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Retro file-based routing
text: Files become URLs, and +layout.ejs files wrap the pages below them:

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Coming from the npm package?
text: PocketPages v1 is a clean API. Apps written for PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) don't run unchanged. See Moving from PocketPages 0.x.

title: Route and Query Parameters
text: Route parameters come from the URL path. Query parameters come from the query string. v1 keeps them apart.

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: Route parameters
text: Use square brackets in file or folder names to capture a URL segment: pb_pages/ products/ [productId]/ index.ejs reviews/ [reviewId].ejs This handles URLs like /products/123 and /products/123/reviews/456 . Read them through params (the same object as ctx.params ): Product: Review: Route parameters are always strings. ctx.params never includes query parameters.

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: Query parameters
text: Read the query string with ctx.req.query() : /products/123?sort=latest&tag=red&tag=blue Sort by: Tags: ctx.req.query(name) First value as a string, or undefined ctx.req.query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings ctx.req.query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter Values are strings. Nothing is parsed for you; if you pass JSON in a query parameter, parse it yourself: const filters = JSON.parse(ctx.req.query('filters') ?? '{}')

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: The route itself
text: ctx.route describes the matched route: { path, name, file } . For products/[productId]/index.ejs , path is /products/[productId] , name is index , and file is products/[productId]/index.ejs .

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
text: Partials are reusable templates that you include from other templates. They live in _private/ folders, which are never routed.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Including a partial
text: include(name, locals?) renders a template from a _private/ folder and returns its text. Use throws if title wasn't passed, but doesn't. Including more than 32 levels deep is an error.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Where partials are found
text: pb_pages/ _private/ header.ejs footer.ejs blog/ _private/ sidebar.ejs posts/ _private/ post-card.ejs index.ejs PocketPages looks in _private/ in the current template's folder, then in each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ : The extension is optional. A dotted name such as include('nav.main') finds nav.main.ejs . This means you can: Keep section-specific partials in that section's _private/ . Hoist a shared partial up to a common parent. Override a parent's partial with a local one of the same name, and still reach the root one with /name .

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Passing data
text: Pass only what the partial needs: Joined Partials can also read ctx , data and params directly. Passing values explicitly keeps them easy to reuse.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Markdown partials
text: A .md partial is rendered as EJS, then Markdown:

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: JavaScript modules
text: _private/ folders also hold JS modules. Load them with ctx.resolve() , which uses the same lookup.

title: Authentication Plugin
text: The auth plugin gives you cookie sessions on PocketBase auth. It calls the app directly, not over HTTP. // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth'], }

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: What it does on every request
text: It reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token and sets ctx.auth to the authenticated record. A bad cookie is cleared. ctx.auth is also set without the plugin when a request carries PocketBase's own Authorization header.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: ctx.session
text: register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }?) Create an auth record. data holds extra fields. verify sends the verification email; signIn signs the new account in (returns { token: '', record } when false ). signInWithPassword(email, password, { collection }?) Sign in with a password. requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }?) Send a one-time password. Returns the otpId . An unknown email still gets an id, one that never validates; with create: true the account is created first. signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }?) Sign in with a one-time password. signInAnonymously({ collection }?) Sign in as a new anonymous user. requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }?) Store state in a cookie and return the provider's URL. With redirect it also sends the redirect; pass redirect: false to send the URL some other way. redirectPath must be a path on this site. signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?) Complete an OAuth2 sign-in on the redirect path. Returns { token, record, meta } ; meta.isNew is true for a new account. signIn(record) Set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. It skips the MFA check below. signOut() Sign out. authMethods({ collection }?) The sign-in methods a collection has turned on: { password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } } , as PocketBase's auth-methods API.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: MFA
text: Pages doesn't have a second sign-in step yet. If a collection has MFA turned on (Collections → users → Options → Multi-factor authentication) and its MFA rule matches the account, every sign-in method above refuses it with "This account needs a second sign-in step (MFA), which pages doesn't support yet." An empty rule matches every account. To use pages sign-in, turn MFA off for the collection, or give it a rule that leaves out the accounts that sign in here. Every sign-in method sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request and returns { token, record } .

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: Email flows
text: These use PocketBase's own checks and mail templates. The request methods never reveal whether an email exists. requestVerification(email, { collection }?) Send the verification email (skipped for an account that's already verified). confirmVerification(token) Mark the account verified. Returns the record. requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }?) Send the password reset email. confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm) Set the new password (and mark the account verified). Returns the record. requestEmailChange(newEmail) Send a confirmation email to newEmail . Needs a signed-in user ( ctx.auth ). confirmEmailChange(token, password) Change the email after checking the current password. Returns the record. A bad or expired token throws an error.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: Example
text: // pb_pages/login/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password) } catch (e) { return { error: 'Invalid email or password', email } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } // pb_pages/logout/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } See the Authentication guide for complete flows: registration, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sign-in.

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
text: A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks: // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'my-plugin', onRequest(ctx) {}, // before middleware extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () = 'hi' }, transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html }, // after each template or layout renders }) Turn it on in +config.js : module.exports = { plugins: ['my-plugin'], // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js }

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: config
text: config is the plugin's entry in +config.js when that entry is an object ( { factory, ...options } ), else {} : module.exports = { plugins: [{ factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Beta' }], } // pb_pages/_private/banner.js module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'banner', transform({ html }) { return html.replace(' ', ${config.text} ) }, })

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Hooks
text: Every hook is optional. Hooks run in the order plugins are listed in +config.js . name The plugin's name. onRequest(ctx) At the start of each request, before middleware. extendContext(ctx) Add members to ctx . transform({ html, ctx, file }) After each template or layout renders. Return the new HTML.

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Example: a context helper
text: module.exports = () = ({ name: 'format', extendContext(ctx) { ctx.formatDate = (d) = new Date(d).toLocaleDateString() }, }) Posted

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Permissions
text: JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS. Under a multitenant host, that means the instance's sandbox.

title: Datastar Add-on
text: The Datastar add-on adds helpers for Datastar. It's a JS plugin that ships with PocketPages rather than a built-in: copy addons/datastar.js into pb_pages/_private/ (the datastar starter kit already has it) and list it in +config.js by name: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['datastar'], } Add the script tags to your root layout's . They load Datastar v1.0.5. Datastar 1.0 uses a colon between the attribute name and its key ( data-on:click , data-bind:name , data-signals:count , data-class:active , data-attr:href ); the older hyphen form ( data-on-click ) is ignored. See the Datastar attribute reference.

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: ctx.datastar
text: scripts({ spa, realtime }?) Returns the script tags. patchElements(html, { selector, mode, useViewTransition, viewTransitionSelector, namespace }?) Sends a patch-elements SSE event on the current response. mode is outer (default), inner , replace , prepend , append , before , after or remove ; namespace is html (default), svg or mathml . patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?) Sends a patch-signals SSE event (JSON Merge Patch: null removes a signal). executeScript(js, { autoRemove, attributes }?) Sends a script to run in the browser. consoleLog(msg) / consoleError(err) Logs to the browser console. redirect(url) Sends the browser to url (a full page load). A Datastar fetch can't follow ctx.res.redirect , so use this from @get / @post handlers. dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector }?) Fires a CustomEvent on document , or on the elements matching selector . replaceURL(url) Changes the address bar without a navigation ( history.replaceState ). prefetch(urls) Adds speculation rules so the browser prefetches urls . signals() Reads the request's signals as an object: from the datastar query parameter for GET and DELETE, from the body otherwise. readSignals(target) Merges the request's signals into target and returns it (0.x's readSignals(request, target) also works). realtime. Sends the same patches to realtime subscribers. Needs the realtime plugin. Every send also takes eventId and retryDuration (in ms; the default 1000 isn't sent).

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Pages as patches
text: When a request has the Datastar-Request: true header, the rendered page is sent without layouts, as a patchElements event. If the request has a Datastar-Selector header, the patch goes into that element. This is how this site navigates between docs pages: the layout calls so links in the table of contents fetch the page and patch it into #content . Plain left-clicks are intercepted; modified clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt, middle-click), links with a target attribute and links to other origins navigate normally. Back/Forward work, including back to the page you landed on: each page opens at the top, and Back/Forward return you to where you were scrolled.

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Example: a counter
text: Count: // pb_pages/counter/+page.js module.exports = { post(ctx) { const count = (ctx.store('count') 0) + 1 ctx.store('count', count) ctx.datastar.patchElements( ${count} ) }, }

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Example: reading signals
text: module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { name, email } = ctx.datastar.signals() if (!name !email) { ctx.datastar.patchSignals({ error: 'Please fill all fields' }) return } ctx.datastar.patchElements(' Thanks! ') }, }

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Broadcasting
text: With the realtime plugin on, ctx.datastar.realtime. sends patches to every realtime subscriber instead of the current response: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime', 'datastar'] } ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements( ${count} )

title: Plugins
